The mission of the twelve, indicating the extension of Christ’s work, and bringing the disciples more directly into conflict with the rabbis, had excited anew the jealousy of the leaders at Jerusalem. The spies they sent to Capernaum in the early part of His ministry, who had tried to fix on Him the charge of Sabbathbreaking, had been put to confusion; but the rabbis were bent on carrying out their purpose. Now another deputation was sent to watch His movements, and find some accusation against Him.

文士和法利賽人預料在逾越節時能看見耶穌，就佈置網羅陷害祂。但耶穌知道他們的陰謀，沒有赴那一次的節期。於是“有法利賽人和幾個文士，到耶穌那裡聚集。”耶穌既不到他們那裡去，他們就到耶穌這裡來。加利利人一度似乎要接受耶穌為彌賽亞。這麼一來，猶太公會的權勢就要在那一帶地方消滅了。十二個使徒奉差遣出去傳道，說明了基督工做的擴充套件，並使門徒更直接地與拉比們衝突，這就重新激起了耶路撒冷領袖們的忌恨。在耶穌起初傳道時，他們派到迦百農去的奸細，曾想控告祂干犯安息日，結果只得狼狽而退。但拉比們非達到目的不可的。於是又派了幾個人去監視耶穌的行動，要找把柄控告祂。

文士和法利赛人预料在逾越节时能看见耶稣，就布置网罗陷害祂。但耶稣知道他们的阴谋，没有赴那一次的节期。于是“有法利赛人和几个文士，到耶稣那里聚集。”耶稣既不到他们那里去，他们就到耶稣这里来。加利利人一度似乎要接受耶稣为弥赛亚。这么一来，犹太公会的权势就要在那一带地方消灭了。十二个使徒奉差遣出去传道，说明了基督工做的扩展，并使门徒更直接地与拉比们冲突，这就重新激起了耶路撒冷领袖们的忌恨。在耶稣起初传道时，他们派到迦百农去的奸细，曾想控告祂干犯安息日，结果只得狼狈而退。但拉比们非达到目的不可的。于是又派了几个人去监视耶稣的行动，要找把柄控告祂。

As before, the ground of complaint was His disregard of the traditional precepts that encumbered the law of God. These were professedly designed to guard the observance of the law, but they were regarded as more sacred than the law itself. When they came in collision with the commandments given from Sinai, preference was given to the rabbinical precepts.
像過去一樣，他們控告耶穌的理由，是因為祂不尊重那些妨礙上帝律法的遺傳條例。在名義上，這些遺傳原是為維護上帝的律法，但實際上他們卻認為遺傳比上帝的律法還要神聖。遇有遺傳與上帝在西奈山所頒佈的誡命相牴觸時，拉比們的規條總是佔優先。
像过去一样，他们控告耶稣的理由，是因为祂不尊重那些妨碍上帝律法的遗传条例。在名义上，这些遗传原是为维护上帝的律法，但实际上他们却认为遗传比上帝的律法还要神圣。遇有遗传与上帝在西奈山所颁布的诫命相抵触时，拉比们的规条总是占优先。

Among the observances most strenuously enforced was that of ceremonial purification. A neglect of the forms to be observed before eating was accounted a heinous sin, to be punished both in this world and in the next; and it was regarded as a virtue to destroy the transgressor.
在各種禮節中，遵守得最嚴格的乃是儀文上的清潔。吃飯前若忽略應守的禮節，就算是大罪，今生來生都要受到刑罰；而且把犯罪的人除滅，算是一件德行。
在各种礼节中，遵守得最严格的乃是仪文上的清洁。吃饭前若忽略应守的礼节，就算是大罪，今生来生都要受到刑罚；而且把犯罪的人除灭，算是一件德行。

The rules in regard to purification were numberless. The period of a lifetime was scarcely sufficient for one to learn them all. The life of those who tried to observe the rabbinical requirements was one long struggle against ceremonial defilement, an endless round of washings and purifications. While the people were occupied with trifling distinctions, and observances which God had not required, their attention was turned away from the great principles of His law.
有關潔淨的規條多得不可勝數，盡一生的光陰去學，也難以全部學會。那些想要遵守拉比教條的人，生活異常艱苦；為要避免儀式方面的汙穢，他們須忍受長期的煩惱，從事無休止的洗濯。當人在這些非上帝所吩咐的煩瑣禮節上消耗精神時，他們就無法注意到上帝律法的基本原則了。
有关洁净的规条多得不可胜数，尽一生的光阴去学，也难以全部学会。那些想要遵守拉比教条的人，生活异常艰苦；为要避免仪式方面的污秽，他们须忍受长期的烦恼，从事无休止的洗濯。当人在这些非上帝所吩咐的烦琐礼节上消耗精神时，他们就无法注意到上帝律法的基本原则了。

Christ and His disciples did not observe these ceremonial washings, and the spies made this neglect the ground of their accusation. They did not, however, make a direct attack on Christ, but came to Him with criticism of His disciples. In the presence of the multitude they said, “Why do Thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.”
基督和祂的門徒並沒有遵守這些洗濯的儀式。奸細們就拿住這一點作為控告的根據。然而他們沒有直接攻擊基督，只是到祂面前批評祂的門徒。他們當著眾人說：“你的門徒為什麼犯古人的遺傳呢？因為吃飯的時候他們不洗手。”
基督和祂的门徒并没有遵守这些洗濯的仪式。奸细们就拿住这一点作为控告的根据。然而他们没有直接攻击基督，只是到祂面前批评祂的门徒。他们当着众人说：“你的门徒为什么犯古人的遗传呢？因为吃饭的时候他们不洗手。”

Whenever the message of truth comes home to souls with special power, Satan stirs up his agents to start a dispute over some minor question. Thus he seeks to attract attention from the real issue. Whenever a good work is begun, there are cavilers ready to enter into dispute over forms or technicalities, to draw minds away from the living realities. When it appears that God is about to work in a special manner for His people, let them not be enticed into a controversy that will work only ruin of souls. The questions that most concern us are, Do I believe with saving faith on the Son of God? Is my life in harmony with the divine law? “He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life.” “And hereby we do know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments.” John 3:36; 1 John 2:3.

每逢真理的資訊以特別的能力感動人心的時候，撒但總要唆使黨羽在瑣碎的問題上進行爭辯。他想借此吸引人的心思，使他們無暇顧及問題的主要關鍵。每逢有人發動善工，總有吹毛求疵的人乘機而入，為形式或手續問題引起爭論，藉此使人的思想脫離活的現實。在上帝行將用特別的方式為祂子民作工的時候，他們萬不可中撒但的詭計而互相爭論，以致他人因而跌倒。那於我們各人最有關係的問題是：我是否以得救的信心信賴上帝的兒子呢？我的人生是否與上帝的律法相符？“信子的人有永生，不信子的人得不著永生。”“我門若遵守祂的誡命，就曉得是認識祂”（約3:36；約壹2:3）。

每逢真理的信息以特别的能力感动人心的时候，撒但总要唆使党羽在琐碎的问题上进行争辩。他想借此吸引人的心思，使他们无暇顾及问题的主要关键。每逢有人发动善工，总有吹毛求疵的人乘机而入，为形式或手续问题引起争论，借此使人的思想脱离活的现实。在上帝行将用特别的方式为祂子民作工的时候，他们万不可中撒但的诡计而互相争论，以致他人因而跌倒。那于我们各人最有关系的问题是：我是否以得救的信心信赖上帝的儿子呢？我的人生是否与上帝的律法相符？“信子的人有永生，不信子的人得不着永生。”“我门若遵守祂的诫命，就晓得是认识祂”（约3:36；约壹2:3）。

Jesus made no attempt to defend Himself or His disciples. He made no reference to the charges against Him, but proceeded to show the spirit that actuated these sticklers for human rites. He gave them an example of what they were repeatedly doing, and had done just before coming in search of Him. “Full well ye reject the commandment of God,” He said, “that ye may keep your own tradition. For Moses said, Honor thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death: but ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free. And ye suffer him no more to do aught for his father or his mother.” They set aside the fifth commandment as of no consequence, but were very exact in carrying out the traditions of the elders. They taught the people that the devotion of their property to the temple was a duty more sacred than even the support of their parents; and that, however great the necessity, it was sacrilege to impart to father or mother any part of what had been thus consecrated. An undutiful child had only to pronounce the word “Corban” over his property, thus devoting it to God, and he could retain it for his own use during his lifetime, and after his death it was to be appropriated to the temple service. Thus he was at liberty, both in life and in death, to dishonor and defraud his parents, under cover of a pretended devotion to God.

耶穌沒有試圖為自己和門徒辯護，也沒有提到他們加在祂身上的罪名，卻揭露這些拘泥形式主義的人所有的動機。祂舉出他們所經常行慣，並在這次來找祂之前方才行過的事作為一個例子。祂說：“你們誠然是廢棄上帝的誡命，要守自己的遺傳。摩西說：‘孝敬父母。’又說：‘咒罵父母的必治死他。’你們倒說：人若對父母說，我所當奉給你的，已經做了各耳板，各耳板就是供獻的意思，以後你們就不容他再奉養父母。”他們把第五條誡命撇在一邊，認為無關重要，卻嚴格地奉行古人的遺傳。他們教訓眾人說，把財產獻給聖殿，比奉養父母的責任更為神聖，而且無論父母的需要多麼緊急，人若將已經獻給聖殿的財物給了父母，就算是犯了褻瀆的罪名。一個不孝的兒子，只要宣告他的財產已經做了“各耳板”獻給上帝，那麼他就可以保留一切為自己一生享用，死後則充作聖殿的公產。這樣，他或生或死，都可以假借侍奉上帝的名義，任意不孝敬並虧負父母了。

耶稣没有试图为自己和门徒辩护，也没有提到他们加在祂身上的罪名，却揭露这些拘泥形式主义的人所有的动机。祂举出他们所经常行惯，并在这次来找祂之前方才行过的事作为一个例子。祂说：“你们诚然是废弃上帝的诫命，要守自己的遗传。摩西说：‘孝敬父母。’又说：‘咒骂父母的必治死他。’你们倒说：人若对父母说，我所当奉给你的，已经做了各耳板，各耳板就是供献的意思，以后你们就不容他再奉养父母。”他们把第五条诫命撇在一边，认为无关重要，却严格地奉行古人的遗传。他们教训众人说，把财产献给圣殿，比奉养父母的责任更为神圣，而且无论父母的需要多么紧急，人若将已经献给圣殿的财物给了父母，就算是犯了亵渎的罪名。一个不孝的儿子，只要声明他的财产已经做了“各耳板”献给上帝，那么他就可以保留一切为自己一生享用，死后则充作圣殿的公产。这样，他或生或死，都可以假借侍奉上帝的名义，任意不孝敬并亏负父母了。

Never, by word or deed, did Jesus lessen man’s obligation to present gifts and offerings to God. It was Christ who gave all the directions of the law in regard to tithes and offerings. When on earth He commended the poor woman who gave her all to the temple treasury. But the apparent zeal for God on the part of the priests and rabbis was a pretense to cover their desire for self-aggrandizement. The people were deceived by them. They were bearing heavy burdens which God had not imposed. Even the disciples of Christ were not wholly free from the yoke that had been bound upon them by inherited prejudice and rabbinical authority. Now, by revealing the true spirit of the rabbis, Jesus sought to free from the bondage of tradition all who were really desirous of serving God.

耶穌從來沒有在言語或行為上減輕世人向上帝奉獻禮物和捐款的義務。律法中有關十分之一和捐款的指示，原是基督親自頒佈的。祂在世時曾稱讚那將一切所有投入聖殿庫中的窮寡婦。但祭司和拉比們所表現對上帝的熱心，無非是一種偽裝，用來掩飾增高自己地位的慾望而已。民眾受了他們的愚弄，負了上帝所未曾加在他們身上的重軛。連基督的門徒也未能完全擺脫這種遺傳的成見，和拉比們的權威所加在他們身上的束縛。現在耶穌揭穿了拉比們的真面目，想借此將一切願意誠心侍奉上帝的人從遺傳的奴役之下解放出來。

耶稣从来没有在言语或行为上减轻世人向上帝奉献礼物和捐款的义务。律法中有关十分之一和捐款的指示，原是基督亲自颁布的。祂在世时曾称赞那将一切所有投入圣殿库中的穷寡妇。但祭司和拉比们所表现对上帝的热心，无非是一种伪装，用来掩饰增高自己地位的欲望而已。民众受了他们的愚弄，负了上帝所未曾加在他们身上的重轭。连基督的门徒也未能完全摆脱这种遗传的成见，和拉比们的权威所加在他们身上的束缚。现在耶稣揭穿了拉比们的真面目，想借此将一切愿意诚心侍奉上帝的人从遗传的奴役之下解放出来。

“Ye hypocrites,” He said, addressing the wily spies, “well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto Me with their mouth, and honoreth Me with their lips; but their heart is far from Me. But in vain they do worship Me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.” The words of Christ were an arraignment of the whole system of Pharisaism. He declared that by placing their requirements above the divine precepts the rabbis were setting themselves above God.
耶穌對那些狡猾的奸細說：“假冒為善的人哪，以賽亞指著你們說的預言，是不錯的。他就：‘這百姓用嘴唇尊敬我，心卻遠離我，他們將人的吩咐，當作道理教導人，所以拜我也是枉然。’”基督的話，乃是對法利賽人全部教義的譴責。祂聲稱拉比們把自己的規條放在上帝的誡命之上，無異是抬舉自己高過上帝。
耶稣对那些狡猾的奸细说：“假冒为善的人哪，以赛亚指着你们说的预言，是不错的。他就：‘这百姓用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我，他们将人的吩咐，当作道理教导人，所以拜我也是枉然。’”基督的话，乃是对法利赛人全部教义的谴责。祂声称拉比们把自己的规条放在上帝的诫命之上，无异是抬举自己高过上帝。

The deputies from Jerusalem were filled with rage. They could not accuse Christ as a violator of the law given from Sinai, for He spoke as its defender against their traditions. The great precepts of the law, which He had presented, appeared in striking contrast to the petty rules that men had devised.
於是這些從耶路撒冷派來的奸細怒氣填胸。他們不能控告基督違犯那在西奈山上頒佈的律法，因為祂所說的話表明祂擁護律法而反對他們的遺傳。祂所提出律法中的偉大律例，和人所制訂的瑣碎規條，相形之下，卻是一個鮮明的對比。
于是这些从耶路撒冷派来的奸细怒气填胸。他们不能控告基督违犯那在西奈山上颁布的律法，因为祂所说的话表明祂拥护律法而反对他们的遗传。祂所提出律法中的伟大律例，和人所制订的琐碎规条，相形之下，却是一个鲜明的对比。

To the multitude, and afterward more fully to His disciples, Jesus explained that defilement comes not from without, but from within. Purity and impurity pertain to the soul. It is the evil deed, the evil word, the evil thought, the transgression of the law of God, not the neglect of external, man-made ceremonies, that defiles a man.
當時耶穌就對眾人解釋，汙穢不是從外面進去，而是從裡面出來的。後來祂又向門徒更詳細地解釋這事。潔淨和不潔淨是屬於心靈的問題。那足以汙穢人的，乃是邪惡的行為，邪惡的言語，邪惡的思想和違犯上帝律法的事，而不是疏忽人為的外表儀式。
当时耶稣就对众人解释，污秽不是从外面进去，而是从里面出来的。后来祂又向门徒更详细地解释这事。洁净和不洁净是属于心灵的问题。那足以污秽人的，乃是邪恶的行为，邪恶的言语，邪恶的思想和违犯上帝律法的事，而不是疏忽人为的外表仪式。

The disciples noted the rage of the spies as their false teaching was exposed. They saw the angry looks, and heard the half-muttered words of dissatisfaction and revenge. Forgetting how often Christ had given evidence that He read the heart as an open book, they told Him of the effect of His words. Hoping that He might conciliate the enraged officials, they said to Jesus, “Knowest Thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?”
門徒注意那些奸細因自己的假教訓被揭穿而動怒。他們看見這些人的怒容，並聽見這些人不滿和含報復之意的竊竊私語。他們忘記了基督曾屢次顯明祂能洞察人心，如同展開的書卷，卻向祂提出祂這次說話所產生的影響。他們希望祂能安撫那些忿怒的官長，就對祂說：“法利賽人聽見這話不服，你知道嗎？”
门徒注意那些奸细因自己的假教训被揭穿而动怒。他们看见这些人的怒容，并听见这些人不满和含报复之意的窃窃私语。他们忘记了基督曾屡次显明祂能洞察人心，如同展开的书卷，却向祂提出祂这次说话所产生的影响。他们希望祂能安抚那些忿怒的官长，就对祂说：“法利赛人听见这话不服，你知道吗？”

He answered, “Every plant, which My heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” The customs and traditions so highly valued by the rabbis were of this world, not from heaven. However great their authority with the people, they could not endure the testing of God. Every human invention that has been substituted for the commandments of God will be found worthless in that day when “God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” Ecclesiastes 12:14.
“耶穌回答說：凡栽種的物，若不是我天父栽種的，必要拔出來。”拉比們這麼重視的風俗和遺傳是屬於這個世界，而不是從天上來的。他們在民間的權威無論多麼大，總經不起上帝的試驗。當“人所做的事，連一切隱藏的事，無論是善是惡，上帝都必審問”的日子（傳12:14），人所用來代替上帝誡命的巧計全必歸於無用。
“耶稣回答说：凡栽种的物，若不是我天父栽种的，必要拔出来。”拉比们这么重视的风俗和遗传是属于这个世界，而不是从天上来的。他们在民间的权威无论多么大，总经不起上帝的试验。当“人所做的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，上帝都必审问”的日子（传12:14），人所用来代替上帝诫命的巧计全必归于无用。

The substitution of the precepts of men for the commandments of God has not ceased. Even among Christians are found institutions and usages that have no better foundation than the traditions of the fathers. Such institutions, resting upon mere human authority, have supplanted those of divine appointment. Men cling to their traditions, and revere their customs, and cherish hatred against those who seek to show them their error. In this day, when we are bidden to call attention to the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, we see the same enmity as was manifested in the days of Christ. Of the remnant people of God it is written, “The dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” Revelation 12:17.

拿人的教訓來代替上帝誡命的事至今仍未停止。就是在基督徒當中，也有種種制度和習慣，其根源無非是祖先的遺傳而已。這些僅僅建立在人的權威之上的制度，竟已代替了上帝所定的制度。人拘守他們的遺傳，尊重自己的風俗，對於那些想要指出他們錯誤的，反而存仇恨的心。今日上帝吩咐我們叫人注意上帝的誡命和耶穌的真道。我們也看見人表現仇恨，正像基督的時代一樣。關於上帝的餘民，經上記著說：“龍向婦人發怒，去與她其餘的兒女爭戰，這兒女就是那守上帝誡命，為耶穌作見證的”（啟12:17）。

拿人的教训来代替上帝诫命的事至今仍未停止。就是在基督徒当中，也有种种制度和习惯，其根源无非是祖先的遗传而已。这些仅仅建立在人的权威之上的制度，竟已代替了上帝所定的制度。人拘守他们的遗传，尊重自己的风俗，对于那些想要指出他们错误的，反而存仇恨的心。今日上帝吩咐我们叫人注意上帝的诫命和耶稣的真道。我们也看见人表现仇恨，正像基督的时代一样。关于上帝的余民，经上记着说：“龙向妇人发怒，去与她其余的儿女争战，这儿女就是那守上帝诫命，为耶稣作见证的”（启12:17）。

But “every plant, which My heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” In place of the authority of the so-called fathers of the church, God bids us accept the word of the eternal Father, the Lord of heaven and earth. Here alone is truth unmixed with error. David said, “I have more understanding than all my teachers: for Thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients, because I keep Thy precepts.” Psalm 119:99, 100. Let all who accept human authority, the customs of the church, or the traditions of the fathers, take heed to the warning conveyed in the words of Christ, “In vain they do worship Me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

但是“凡栽種的物，若不是我天父栽種的，必要拔出來。”上帝吩咐我們接受永生之父，天地之主的話，不要我們聽從所謂教會父老的威權。只有如此，真理才不致與錯謬混為一談。大衛說：“我比我的師傅更通達，因我思想你的法度。我比年老的更明白，因我守了你的訓詞”（詩119:99,100）。基督說：“他們將人的吩咐，當作道理教導人，所以拜我也是枉然”。願一切接受世人的威權，教會的風俗，或父老的遺傳的人，注意耶穌這話所含的警告。

但是“凡栽种的物，若不是我天父栽种的，必要拔出来。”上帝吩咐我们接受永生之父，天地之主的话，不要我们听从所谓教会父老的威权。只有如此，真理才不致与错谬混为一谈。大卫说：“我比我的师傅更通达，因我思想你的法度。我比年老的更明白，因我守了你的训词”（诗119:99,100）。基督说：“他们将人的吩咐，当作道理教导人，所以拜我也是枉然”。愿一切接受世人的威权，教会的风俗，或父老的遗传的人，注意耶稣这话所含的警告。
Chapter 43—Barriers Broken Down
消除種族的歧視
消除种族的歧视

This chapter is based on Matthew 15:21-28; Mark 7:24-30.
After the encounter with the Pharisees, Jesus withdrew from Capernaum, and crossing Galilee, repaired to the hill country on the borders of Phoenicia. Looking westward, He could see, spread out upon the plain below, the ancient cities of Tyre and Sidon, with their heathen temples, their magnificent palaces and marts of trade, and the harbors filled with shipping. Beyond was the blue expanse of the Mediterranean, over which the messengers of the gospel were to bear its glad tidings to the centers of the world’s great empire. But the time was not yet. The work before Him now was to prepare His disciples for their mission. In coming to this region He hoped to find the retirement He had failed to secure at Bethsaida. Yet this was not His only purpose in taking this journey.

耶穌和法利賽人辯論一番之後，就離開迦百農，經過加利利到腓尼基邊境的山地去。從那裡舉目西望，祂可以看見下面平原上的兩座古城，推羅和西頓。城裡有異教的廟宇，壯麗的宮殿，繁盛的市場和停滿船隻的海港。再望過去，便是蔚藍的地中海。福音的使者將來要渡過這茫茫的大海，把大喜的資訊，傳到羅馬帝國的各中心地區。然而時機還未成熟。耶穌當前的工作，乃是準備門徒擔負他們的使命。祂到這一帶地方，希望能找到在伯賽大被打攪了的休息。然而這並不是祂這次旅行的唯一目的。

耶稣和法利赛人辩论一番之后，就离开迦百农，经过加利利到腓尼基边境的山地去。从那里举目西望，祂可以看见下面平原上的两座古城，推罗和西顿。城里有异教的庙宇，壮丽的宫殿，繁盛的市场和停满船只的海港。再望过去，便是蔚蓝的地中海。福音的使者将来要渡过这茫茫的大海，把大喜的信息，传到罗马帝国的各中心地区。然而时机还未成熟。耶稣当前的工作，乃是准备门徒担负他们的使命。祂到这一带地方，希望能找到在伯赛大被打搅了的休息。然而这并不是祂这次旅行的唯一目的。

“Behold, a Canaanitish woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, Thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.” Matthew 15:22, R. V. The people of this district were of the old Canaanite race. They were idolaters, and were despised and hated by the Jews. To this class belonged the woman who now came to Jesus. She was a heathen, and was therefore excluded from the advantages which the Jews daily enjoyed. There were many Jews living among the Phoenicians, and the tidings of Christ’s work had penetrated to this region. Some of the people had listened to His words and had witnessed His wonderful works. This woman had heard of the prophet, who, it was reported, healed all manner of diseases. As she heard of His power, hope sprang up in her heart. Inspired by a mother’s love, she determined to present her daughter’s case to Him. It was her resolute purpose to bring her affliction to Jesus. He must heal her child. She had sought help from the heathen gods, but had obtained no relief. And at times she was tempted to think, What can this Jewish teacher do for me? But the word had come, He heals all manner of diseases, whether those who come to Him for help are rich or poor. She determined not to lose her only hope.

“有一個迦南婦人，從那地方出來，喊著說：主啊！大衛的子孫，可憐我，我女兒被鬼附得甚苦。”這地方的居民屬於古迦南族。他們是拜偶像的，為猶太人所鄙視所憎惡。現在來求耶穌的婦人，就是這一等人。她是個異教徒，所以不能享受猶太人經常所享的權利。當時有許多猶太人雜居在腓尼基人之間，所以基督工做的訊息已經傳到這一帶地方了。其中有一些人曾聽過耶穌講道，並親眼見過祂行奇事。這個婦人曾經聽說過這位先知能醫治各種疾病。當她聽人講說耶穌的大能時，她心裡不禁生出希望來。她為母愛所激動，決意求祂醫治她女兒的病症。她堅決要把自己的苦情告訴耶穌，非要祂醫治她的女兒不可。她曾經向邪神求告，並未見效，所以她有時不免疑問：這位猶太的教師能為我做什麼呢？但她聽說耶穌確能醫治各種疾病。凡向祂求助的，不論貧富，祂都一視同仁。於是她決意不放過她唯一的希望。

“有一个迦南妇人，从那地方出来，喊着说：主啊！大卫的子孙，可怜我，我女儿被鬼附得甚苦。”这地方的居民属于古迦南族。他们是拜偶像的，为犹太人所鄙视所憎恶。现在来求耶稣的妇人，就是这一等人。她是个异教徒，所以不能享受犹太人经常所享的权利。当时有许多犹太人杂居在腓尼基人之间，所以基督工做的消息已经传到这一带地方了。其中有一些人曾听过耶稣讲道，并亲眼见过祂行奇事。这个妇人曾经听说过这位先知能医治各种疾病。当她听人讲说耶稣的大能时，她心里不禁生出希望来。她为母爱所激动，决意求祂医治她女儿的病症。她坚决要把自己的苦情告诉耶稣，非要祂医治她的女儿不可。她曾经向邪神求告，并未见效，所以她有时不免疑问：这位犹太的教师能为我做什么呢？但她听说耶稣确能医治各种疾病。凡向祂求助的，不论贫富，祂都一视同仁。于是她决意不放过她唯一的希望。

Christ knew this woman’s situation. He knew that she was longing to see Him, and He placed Himself in her path. By ministering to her sorrow, He could give a living representation of the lesson He designed to teach. For this He had brought His disciples into this region. He desired them to see the ignorance existing in cities and villages close to the land of Israel. The people who had been given every opportunity to understand the truth were without a knowledge of the needs of those around them. No effort was made to help souls in darkness. The partition wall which Jewish pride had erected, shut even the disciples from sympathy with the heathen world. But these barriers were to be broken down.
基督明白這婦人的景況，並知道她渴望見祂，所以特地來與她相遇。基督打算藉著解除她的憂患，為祂所要給人的教訓作一個活的說明。祂把門徒帶到這一帶地方來，正是為此。祂要他們看到鄰近以色列的城市鄉村中所存在愚昧無知的狀況。那曾有種種機會明白真理的以色列民，卻不知道周圍人群的需要，也不出力幫助在黑暗裡的生靈。猶太人的驕傲所造成的隔牆，竟使耶穌的門徒也不對異邦人表示同情。但這種種族的歧視，是必須予以消除的。
基督明白这妇人的景况，并知道她渴望见祂，所以特地来与她相遇。基督打算借着解除她的忧患，为祂所要给人的教训作一个活的说明。祂把门徒带到这一带地方来，正是为此。祂要他们看到邻近以色列的城市乡村中所存在愚昧无知的状况。那曾有种种机会明白真理的以色列民，却不知道周围人群的需要，也不出力帮助在黑暗里的生灵。犹太人的骄傲所造成的隔墙，竟使耶稣的门徒也不对异邦人表示同情。但这种种族的歧视，是必须予以消除的。

Christ did not immediately reply to the woman’s request. He received this representative of a despised race as the Jews would have done. In this He designed that His disciples should be impressed with the cold and heartless manner in which the Jews would treat such a case, as evinced by His reception of the woman, and the compassionate manner in which He would have them deal with such distress, as manifested by His subsequent granting of her petition.
基督沒有立刻應允婦人的要求。祂照猶太人的習慣來對待這被輕視之民族的婦人。耶穌要門徒先從祂對待婦人的態度上，看出猶太人在同樣情形之下所有冷酷無情的作風，再從祂以後應允婦人的請求上，體會到耶穌要他們對這種苦惱的人所應表示的仁慈。
基督没有立刻应允妇人的要求。祂照犹太人的习惯来对待这被轻视之民族的妇人。耶稣要门徒先从祂对待妇人的态度上，看出犹太人在同样情形之下所有冷酷无情的作风，再从祂以后应允妇人的请求上，体会到耶稣要他们对这种苦恼的人所应表示的仁慈。

But although Jesus did not reply, the woman did not lose faith. As He passed on, as if not hearing her, she followed Him, continuing her supplications. Annoyed by her importunities, the disciples asked Jesus to send her away. They saw that their Master treated her with indifference, and they therefore supposed that the prejudice of the Jews against the Canaanites was pleasing to Him. But it was a pitying Saviour to whom the woman made her plea, and in answer to the request of the disciples, Jesus said, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Although this answer appeared to be in accordance with the prejudice of the Jews, it was an implied rebuke to the disciples, which they afterward understood as reminding them of what He had often told them,—that He came to the world to save all who would accept Him.

耶穌雖然沒有答覆，但婦人並沒有失去信心。耶穌似乎沒有聽見她喊叫，只管向前走， 她卻跟在後面不斷地懇求。門徒因她纏擾不休甚為厭煩，就請耶穌打發她走開。他們看見夫子對她漠不關心，就以為猶太人對於迦南人的歧視也是耶穌所讚許的。但婦人所求的乃是慈憐的救主。耶穌答覆門徒的要求說：“我奉差遣，不過是到以色列家迷失的羊那裡去。”這個回答雖然聽起來似乎符合猶太人的成見，但其實含有譴責門徒的意思，使他們後來明白這是提醒他們耶穌所常常告訴他們的話：祂到世上來為要拯救凡願意接受祂的人。

耶稣虽然没有答复，但妇人并没有失去信心。耶稣似乎没有听见她喊叫，只管向前走， 她却跟在后面不断地恳求。门徒因她缠扰不休甚为厌烦，就请耶稣打发她走开。他们看见夫子对她漠不关心，就以为犹太人对于迦南人的歧视也是耶稣所赞许的。但妇人所求的乃是慈怜的救主。耶稣答复门徒的要求说：“我奉差遣，不过是到以色列家迷失的羊那里去。”这个回答虽然听起来似乎符合犹太人的成见，但其实含有谴责门徒的意思，使他们后来明白这是提醒他们耶稣所常常告诉他们的话：祂到世上来为要拯救凡愿意接受祂的人。

The woman urged her case with increased earnestness, bowing at Christ’s feet, and crying, “Lord, help me.” Jesus, still apparently rejecting her entreaties, according to the unfeeling prejudice of the Jews, answered, “It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.” This was virtually asserting that it was not just to lavish the blessings brought to the favored people of God upon strangers and aliens from Israel. This answer would have utterly discouraged a less earnest seeker. But the woman saw that her opportunity had come. Beneath the apparent refusal of Jesus, she saw a compassion that He could not hide. “Truth, Lord,” she answered, “yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.” While the children of the household eat at the father’s table, even the dogs are not left unfed. They have a right to the crumbs that fall from the table abundantly supplied. So while there were many blessings given to Israel, was there not also a blessing for her? She was looked upon as a dog, and had she not then a dog’s claim to a crumb from His bounty?

那婦人越發誠懇地提出她的要求，俯伏在耶穌腳前，說：“主啊，幫助我。”耶穌顯然仍在照著猶太人冷酷的成見拒絕她的懇求。回答說：“不好拿兒女的餅，丟給狗吃。”就是說，上帝賜給祂所眷愛的子民的恩澤，浪費在與以色列無關的外人身上，是不相宜的。在一個比較不懇切的請求者，耶穌的這種問答足能使他灰心失望的。但婦人卻看出這是她的機會。她看出耶穌表面上雖然拒絕她，但祂內心的慈悲卻是隱藏不住的。於是她回答說：“主啊！不錯，但是狗也吃他主人桌子上掉下來的碎渣兒。”家裡的兒女們固然吃父親的飯，但是狗也不致於捱餓。狗還可以吃那擺滿食物的桌子上所掉下來的碎渣兒。所以以色列人既得到許多福惠，難道沒有一點兒恩惠賜給她嗎？她既被視為一條狗，那麼豈不能從上帝的豐富中取一點碎渣兒嗎？

那妇人越发诚恳地提出她的要求，俯伏在耶稣脚前，说：“主啊，帮助我。”耶稣显然仍在照着犹太人冷酷的成见拒绝她的恳求。回答说：“不好拿儿女的饼，丢给狗吃。”就是说，上帝赐给祂所眷爱的子民的恩泽，浪费在与以色列无关的外人身上，是不相宜的。在一个比较不恳切的请求者，耶稣的这种问答足能使他灰心失望的。但妇人却看出这是她的机会。她看出耶稣表面上虽然拒绝她，但祂内心的慈悲却是隐藏不住的。于是她回答说：“主啊！不错，但是狗也吃他主人桌子上掉下来的碎渣儿。”家里的儿女们固然吃父亲的饭，但是狗也不致于挨饿。狗还可以吃那摆满食物的桌子上所掉下来的碎渣儿。所以以色列人既得到许多福惠，难道没有一点儿恩惠赐给她吗？她既被视为一条狗，那么岂不能从上帝的丰富中取一点碎渣儿吗？

Jesus had just departed from His field of labor because the scribes and Pharisees were seeking to take His life. They murmured and complained. They manifested unbelief and bitterness, and refused the salvation so freely offered them. Here Christ meets one of an unfortunate and despised race, that has not been favored with the light of God’s word; yet she yields at once to the divine influence of Christ, and has implicit faith in His ability to grant the favor she asks. She begs for the crumbs that fall from the Master’s table. If she may have the privilege of a dog, she is willing to be regarded as a dog. She has no national or religious prejudice or pride to influence her course, and she immediately acknowledges Jesus as the Redeemer, and as being able to do all that she asks of Him.

那時，耶穌因為文士和法利賽人尋索祂的命，剛離開祂的工作地點。他們曾心懷不平，口出怨言，顯示不信和毒恨，拒絕那白白賜給他們的救恩。到了這裡，基督遇見一個不幸被輕視之民族的婦人。她未曾受到上帝真道之光的恩惠，但她立時依從基督神聖的感化力，並篤信祂能應允她的要求。她乞求從主人的桌子上所掉下來的碎渣兒。只要能享受到狗的待遇，她願意被看為一條狗。她沒有民族或宗教的成見或驕傲來影響她的行動。她當時就承認耶穌為救贖主，並承認祂能成全她向祂所求的一切。

那时，耶稣因为文士和法利赛人寻索祂的命，刚离开祂的工作地点。他们曾心怀不平，口出怨言，显示不信和毒恨，拒绝那白白赐给他们的救恩。到了这里，基督遇见一个不幸被轻视之民族的妇人。她未曾受到上帝真道之光的恩惠，但她立时依从基督神圣的感化力，并笃信祂能应允她的要求。她乞求从主人的桌子上所掉下来的碎渣儿。只要能享受到狗的待遇，她愿意被看为一条狗。她没有民族或宗教的成见或骄傲来影响她的行动。她当时就承认耶稣为救赎主，并承认祂能成全她向祂所求的一切。

The Saviour is satisfied. He has tested her faith in Him. By His dealings with her, He has shown that she who has been regarded as an outcast from Israel is no longer an alien, but a child in God’s household. As a child it is her privilege to share in the Father’s gifts. Christ now grants her request, and finishes the lesson to the disciples. Turning to her with a look of pity and love, He says, “O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.” From that hour her daughter became whole. The demon troubled her no more. The woman departed, acknowledging her Saviour, and happy in the granting of her prayer.
救主滿意了。祂已經試驗婦人對祂所有的信心。在耶穌對待她的事情上，祂表明這曾經被看為與以色列無關的人已不再是外人，乃是上帝家裡的兒女。既是兒女，她就有權利享受父親的恩賜。於是基督答應她的請求，結束了祂給門徒的教訓。祂帶著憐恤和慈愛的神色轉身對婦人說：“婦人，你的信心是大的，照你所要的，給你成全了吧。”從那時候，她的女兒就好了。鬼也不再纏擾她了。婦人回去，承認她的救主，並因她的懇求得到應允而喜樂。
救主满意了。祂已经试验妇人对祂所有的信心。在耶稣对待她的事情上，祂表明这曾经被看为与以色列无关的人已不再是外人，乃是上帝家里的儿女。既是儿女，她就有权利享受父亲的恩赐。于是基督答应她的请求，结束了祂给门徒的教训。祂带着怜恤和慈爱的神色转身对妇人说：“妇人，你的信心是大的，照你所要的，给你成全了吧。”从那时候，她的女儿就好了。鬼也不再缠扰她了。妇人回去，承认她的救主，并因她的恳求得到应允而喜乐。

This was the only miracle that Jesus wrought while on this journey. It was for the performance of this act that He went to the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He wished to relieve the afflicted woman, and at the same time to leave an example in His work of mercy toward one of a despised people for the benefit of His disciples when He should no longer be with them. He wished to lead them from their Jewish exclusiveness to be interested in working for others besides their own people.
這是耶穌在這次旅程中所行的唯一神蹟。他到推羅西頓的邊境來，也就是為了要行這一件事。祂要解除那婦人的痛苦，同時也要藉著向一個被鄙視之民族的婦人施恩，而為門徒留下一個榜樣，以便將來祂不能與他們同在的時候，他們可以得到幫助。祂要引導他們脫離猶太人的那種排外心理，而樂意為外族的人服務。
这是耶稣在这次旅程中所行的唯一神迹。他到推罗西顿的边境来，也就是为了要行这一件事。祂要解除那妇人的痛苦，同时也要借着向一个被鄙视之民族的妇人施恩，而为门徒留下一个榜样，以便将来祂不能与他们同在的时候，他们可以得到帮助。祂要引导他们脱离犹太人的那种排外心理，而乐意为外族的人服务。

Jesus longed to unfold the deep mysteries of the truth which had been hid for ages, that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs with the Jews, and “partakers of His promise in Christ by the gospel.” Ephesians 3:6. This truth the disciples were slow to learn, and the divine Teacher gave them lesson upon lesson. In rewarding the faith of the centurion at Capernaum, and preaching the gospel to the inhabitants of Sychar, He had already given evidence that He did not share the intolerance of the Jews. But the Samaritans had some knowledge of God; and the centurion had shown kindness to Israel. Now Jesus brought the disciples in contact with a heathen, whom they regarded as having no reason above any of her people, to expect favor from Him. He would give an example of how such a one should be treated. The disciples had thought that He dispensed too freely the gifts of His grace. He would show that His love was not to be circumscribed to race or nation.

耶穌渴望把歷代以來所隱藏的真理奧秘闡明出來，就是外邦人要與猶太人同為後嗣，並“在基督耶穌裡，藉著福音，得以……同蒙應許”（弗3:6）。但這個真理門徒不易領會，所以他們神聖的教師再三地教訓他們。祂曾報賞迦百農百夫長的信心，並傳福音給敍加的居民。在這些事上，祂已經表示不贊同猶太人排外的作風。但撒瑪利亞人究竟對於上帝還有一點認識；百夫長曾優待以色列人。現在耶穌使門徒接觸到一個信邪教的人，在門徒眼中，她不比她同族的任何人更有受耶穌恩待的理由。耶穌就用她作榜樣，使門徒知道應當如何對待這樣的一個人。門徒曾認為耶穌過於浪費祂的恩典。但耶穌卻要表明祂的愛是不可限於任何一個民族或國家的。

耶稣渴望把历代以来所隐藏的真理奥秘阐明出来，就是外邦人要与犹太人同为后嗣，并“在基督耶稣里，借着福音，得以……同蒙应许”（弗3:6）。但这个真理门徒不易领会，所以他们神圣的教师再三地教训他们。祂曾报赏迦百农百夫长的信心，并传福音给敍加的居民。在这些事上，祂已经表示不赞同犹太人排外的作风。但撒玛利亚人究竟对于上帝还有一点认识；百夫长曾优待以色列人。现在耶稣使门徒接触到一个信邪教的人，在门徒眼中，她不比她同族的任何人更有受耶稣恩待的理由。耶稣就用她作榜样，使门徒知道应当如何对待这样的一个人。门徒曾认为耶稣过于浪费祂的恩典。但耶稣却要表明祂的爱是不可限于任何一个民族或国家的。

When He said, “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel,” He stated the truth, and in His work for the Canaanite woman He was fulfilling His commission. This woman was one of the lost sheep that Israel should have rescued. It was their appointed work, the work which they had neglected, that Christ was doing.
“我奉差遣，不過是到以色列家迷失的羊那裡去。”耶穌的這一句話就是真理。祂對那迦南婦人所行的事正是履行祂的使命。這婦人正是以色列人所應當營救的一隻迷失的羊。這原是上帝派給他們的工作。他們既疏忽了責任，基督就替他們做了。
“我奉差遣，不过是到以色列家迷失的羊那里去。”耶稣的这一句话就是真理。祂对那迦南妇人所行的事正是履行祂的使命。这妇人正是以色列人所应当营救的一只迷失的羊。这原是上帝派给他们的工作。他们既疏忽了责任，基督就替他们做了。

This act opened the minds of the disciples more fully to the labor that lay before them among the Gentiles. They saw a wide field of usefulness outside of Judea. They saw souls bearing sorrows unknown to those more highly favored. Among those whom they had been taught to despise were souls longing for help from the mighty Healer, hungering for the light of truth, which had been so abundantly given to the Jews.
這件事使門徒更清楚地認識到那擺在他們面前在外邦人中的工作。他們看出在猶大地以外，有廣大的工作園地，並看到有許多人揹負著那些蒙恩更多的人所不明瞭的憂患。門徒素來所鄙視的外邦人中，有許多渴望蒙“大醫師”幫助的人。他們渴慕上帝所大量給予猶太人的真理之光。
这件事使门徒更清楚地认识到那摆在他们面前在外邦人中的工作。他们看出在犹大地以外，有广大的工作园地，并看到有许多人背负着那些蒙恩更多的人所不明了的忧患。门徒素来所鄙视的外邦人中，有许多渴望蒙“大医师”帮助的人。他们渴慕上帝所大量给予犹太人的真理之光。

Afterward, when the Jews turned still more persistently from the disciples, because they declared Jesus to be the Saviour of the world, and when the partition wall between Jew and Gentile was broken down by the death of Christ, this lesson, and similar ones which pointed to the gospel work unrestricted by custom or nationality, had a powerful influence upon the representatives of Christ, in directing their labors.
後來，當猶太人因門徒宣稱耶穌為世界的救主，而更堅決地反對他們時，當耶穌的死把猶太人和外邦人之間的隔牆拆毀時，這一次的教訓和其他說明福音工作不受風俗或國界之限制的教訓，在引導基督代表們的工作上，起了很大的作用。
后来，当犹太人因门徒宣称耶稣为世界的救主，而更坚决地反对他们时，当耶稣的死把犹太人和外邦人之间的隔墙拆毁时，这一次的教训和其他说明福音工作不受风俗或国界之限制的教训，在引导基督代表们的工作上，起了很大的作用。

The Saviour’s visit to Phoenicia and the miracle there performed had a yet wider purpose. Not alone for the afflicted woman, nor even for His disciples and those who received their labors, was the work accomplished; but also “that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through His name.” John 20:31. The same agencies that barred men away from Christ eighteen hundred years ago are at work today. The spirit which built up the partition wall between Jew and Gentile is still active. Pride and prejudice have built strong walls of separation between different classes of men. Christ and His mission have been misrepresented, and multitudes feel that they are virtually shut away from the ministry of the gospel. But let them not feel that they are shut away from Christ. There are no barriers which man or Satan can erect but that faith can penetrate.

救主這次腓尼基之行和祂在那裡所行的神蹟，還有更遠大的宗旨。祂行這件事，不僅是為了那苦惱的婦人，也不專是為祂的門徒和一般得他們幫助的人，而也是為“要叫你們信耶穌是基督，是上帝的兒子，並且叫你們信了祂，就可以因祂的名得生命”（約20:31）。在一千九百多年前攔阻人就近基督的勢力，如今仍在活動。那時在猶太人和外邦人之間造成隔牆的精神，現在依然盛行。驕傲和偏見造成了堅固的壁壘，把各等各色的人隔開。基督和祂的使命被人曲解，於是許多人覺得自己簡直是被關在福音的門外。但這些人不要以為自己是與基督隔絕了，因為世人或撒但所能造成的任何障礙，總是信心所能打破的。

救主这次腓尼基之行和祂在那里所行的神迹，还有更远大的宗旨。祂行这件事，不仅是为了那苦恼的妇人，也不专是为祂的门徒和一般得他们帮助的人，而也是为“要叫你们信耶稣是基督，是上帝的儿子，并且叫你们信了祂，就可以因祂的名得生命”（约20:31）。在一千九百多年前拦阻人就近基督的势力，如今仍在活动。那时在犹太人和外邦人之间造成隔墙的精神，现在依然盛行。骄傲和偏见造成了坚固的壁垒，把各等各色的人隔开。基督和祂的使命被人曲解，于是许多人觉得自己简直是被关在福音的门外。但这些人不要以为自己是与基督隔绝了，因为世人或撒但所能造成的任何障碍，总是信心所能打破的。

In faith the woman of Phoenicia flung herself against the barriers that had been piled up between Jew and Gentile. Against discouragement, regardless of appearances that might have led her to doubt, she trusted the Saviour’s love. It is thus that Christ desires us to trust in Him. The blessings of salvation are for every soul. Nothing but his own choice can prevent any man from becoming a partaker of the promise in Christ by the gospel.
腓尼基的婦人抱著信心，直向猶太人和外邦人之間所累積的障礙猛撲過去。她冒著失望的威脅，不顧一切足以使她疑惑的現象，一心信靠救主的愛。基督願意我們也要這樣信賴祂。救恩的福惠是賜給每一個人的。除非一個人自己不肯，任何事物都不能攔阻他領受在基督裡藉著福音所賜的應許。
腓尼基的妇人抱着信心，直向犹太人和外邦人之间所累积的障碍猛扑过去。她冒着失望的威胁，不顾一切足以使她疑惑的现象，一心信靠救主的爱。基督愿意我们也要这样信赖祂。救恩的福惠是赐给每一个人的。除非一个人自己不肯，任何事物都不能拦阻他领受在基督里借着福音所赐的应许。

Caste is hateful to God. He ignores everything of this character. In His sight the souls of all men are of equal value. He “hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation; that they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after Him, and find Him, though He be not far from every one of us.” Without distinction of age, or rank, or nationality, or religious privilege, all are invited to come unto Him and live. “Whosoever believeth on Him shall not be ashamed. For there is no difference.” “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free.” “The rich and poor meet together: the Lord is the Maker of them all.” “The same Lord over all is rich unto all that call upon Him. For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Acts 17:26, 27; Galatians 3:28; Proverbs 22:2; Romans 10:11-13.

人所劃分的界限是上帝所恨惡的。祂不承認任何這一類的事。在祂眼中，眾人的靈魂都是一樣可貴的。“祂從一本造出萬族的人，住在全地上，並且預先定準他們的年限和所住的疆界。要叫他們尋求上帝，或者可以揣摩而得，其實祂離我們各人不遠”（徒17:26,27）。不分年齡，階級，國籍，或宗教方面的特權，人人都被請到祂那裡得生命。“凡信祂的人，必不致於羞愧……並沒有份別”（羅10:11,12）。“並不分猶太人，希臘人，自主的，為奴的”（加3:28）。“富戶窮人，在世相遇，都為耶和華所造”（箴22:2）。“眾人同是一位主，祂也厚待一切求告祂的人，因為凡求告主名的，就必得救”（羅10:12,13）。

人所划分的界限是上帝所恨恶的。祂不承认任何这一类的事。在祂眼中，众人的灵魂都是一样可贵的。“祂从一本造出万族的人，住在全地上，并且预先定准他们的年限和所住的疆界。要叫他们寻求上帝，或者可以揣摩而得，其实祂离我们各人不远”（徒17:26,27）。不分年龄，阶级，国籍，或宗教方面的特权，人人都被请到祂那里得生命。“凡信祂的人，必不致于羞愧……并没有份别”（罗10:11,12）。“并不分犹太人，希腊人，自主的，为奴的”（加3:28）。“富户穷人，在世相遇，都为耶和华所造”（箴22:2）。“众人同是一位主，祂也厚待一切求告祂的人，因为凡求告主名的，就必得救”（罗10:12,13）。
Chapter 44—The True Sign
真的神蹟
真的神迹

This chapter is based on Matthew 15:29-39; Matthew 16:1-12;
> Mark 7:31-37; Mark 8:1-21.
“耶穌又離了推羅的境界，經過西頓，就從低加波利境內來到加利利海。”
“耶稣又离了推罗的境界，经过西顿，就从低加波利境内来到加利利海。”

“Again He went out from the borders of Tyre, and came through Sidon unto the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.” Mark 7:31, R. V.
It was in the region of Decapolis that the demoniacs of Gergesa had been healed. Here the people, alarmed at the destruction of the swine, had constrained Jesus to depart from among them. But they had listened to the messengers He left behind, and a desire was aroused to see Him. As He came again into that region, a crowd gathered about Him, and a deaf, stammering man was brought to Him. Jesus did not, according to His custom, restore the man by a word only. Taking him apart from the multitude, He put His fingers in his ears, and touched his tongue; looking up to heaven, He sighed at thought of the ears that would not be open to the truth, the tongues that refused to acknowledge the Redeemer. At the word, “Be opened,” the man’s speech was restored, and, disregarding the command to tell no man, he published abroad the story of his cure.

耶穌醫治格拉森被鬼附的人，是在低加波利境內。這裡的居民因為豬群被淹，心裡恐慌，曾求耶穌離開他們。但他們聽了耶穌留下的兩個治好的瘋子為祂所做的見證，就願意見祂了。這次祂再到這一帶地方來，就有一群人圍著祂。有一個耳聾舌結的人被帶到祂面前。耶穌並沒有照祂的慣例，單說一句話醫好了他。祂領他離開眾人，用指頭探他的耳朵，又摸他的舌頭，於是舉目望天，想到那些有耳不肯聽真理，有舌不肯承認救贖主的人而不禁為之嘆息。祂說：“開了吧！”那人立時恢復了講話的能力。耶穌雖然囑咐他不要告訴人，但他卻將自己蒙醫治的情形到處傳揚開了。

耶稣医治格拉森被鬼附的人，是在低加波利境内。这里的居民因为猪群被淹，心里恐慌，曾求耶稣离开他们。但他们听了耶稣留下的两个治好的疯子为祂所做的见证，就愿意见祂了。这次祂再到这一带地方来，就有一群人围着祂。有一个耳聋舌结的人被带到祂面前。耶稣并没有照祂的惯例，单说一句话医好了他。祂领他离开众人，用指头探他的耳朵，又摸他的舌头，于是举目望天，想到那些有耳不肯听真理，有舌不肯承认救赎主的人而不禁为之叹息。祂说：“开了吧！”那人立时恢复了讲话的能力。耶稣虽然嘱咐他不要告诉人，但他却将自己蒙医治的情形到处传扬开了。

Jesus went up into a mountain, and there the multitude flocked to Him, bringing their sick and lame, and laying them at His feet. He healed them all; and the people, heathen as they were, glorified the God of Israel. For three days they continued to throng about the Saviour, sleeping at night in the open air, and through the day pressing eagerly to hear the words of Christ, and to see His works. At the end of three days their food was spent. Jesus would not send them away hungry, and He called upon His disciples to give them food. Again the disciples revealed their unbelief. At Bethsaida they had seen how, with Christ’s blessing, their little store availed for the feeding of the multitude; yet they did not now bring forward their all, trusting His power to multiply it for the hungry crowds. Moreover, those whom He fed at Bethsaida were Jews; these were Gentiles and heathen. Jewish prejudice was still strong in the hearts of the disciples, and they answered Jesus, “Whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?” But obedient to His word they brought Him what they had,—seven loaves and two fishes. The multitude were fed, seven large baskets of fragments remaining. Four thousand men, besides women and children, were thus refreshed, and Jesus sent them away with glad and grateful hearts.

耶穌上了一座山，眾人蜂擁到祂那裡，把有病的，殘廢的，都帶來放在祂腳前。祂醫好了他們。他們雖是不信主的異教人，卻也歸榮耀給以色列的上帝。他們聚集在救主身邊有三天之久，晚上露天睡覺，白天熱切地擁擠著聽基督的講論，並看祂所行的事。三天之後，他們帶來的食物吃完了。耶穌不願叫他們餓著回去，就吩咐門徒給他們吃。門徒這次又表現出他們的不信。在伯賽大他們曾看見自己所有的一點食物如何經過基督的祝謝，就足以供給眾人吃飽。但這時他們並沒有把所有的食物拿出來，信賴祂的能力能為飢餓的人群使食物增多。況且在伯賽大吃飽的是猶太人，現在這些都是外邦人，異教徒。猶太人的民族偏見這時依然存在門徒心裡。他們就回答耶穌說：“在這野地，從哪裡能得餅，叫這些人吃飽呢？”但他們終於聽從耶穌的話，把所有的食物拿了出來──七個餅，兩條魚。眾人都吃飽了，剩下的零碎，裝滿了七個大筐子。這次得以吃飽而恢復精力的，除了婦孺以外，共有四千人。於是耶穌就遣散這一群人心裡充滿著喜樂和感謝的人。

耶稣上了一座山，众人蜂拥到祂那里，把有病的，残废的，都带来放在祂脚前。祂医好了他们。他们虽是不信主的异教人，却也归荣耀给以色列的上帝。他们聚集在救主身边有三天之久，晚上露天睡觉，白天热切地拥挤着听基督的讲论，并看祂所行的事。三天之后，他们带来的食物吃完了。耶稣不愿叫他们饿着回去，就吩咐门徒给他们吃。门徒这次又表现出他们的不信。在伯赛大他们曾看见自己所有的一点食物如何经过基督的祝谢，就足以供给众人吃饱。但这时他们并没有把所有的食物拿出来，信赖祂的能力能为饥饿的人群使食物增多。况且在伯赛大吃饱的是犹太人，现在这些都是外邦人，异教徒。犹太人的民族偏见这时依然存在门徒心里。他们就回答耶稣说：“在这野地，从哪里能得饼，叫这些人吃饱呢？”但他们终于听从耶稣的话，把所有的食物拿了出来──七个饼，两条鱼。众人都吃饱了，剩下的零碎，装满了七个大筐子。这次得以吃饱而恢复精力的，除了妇孺以外，共有四千人。于是耶稣就遣散这一群人心里充满着喜乐和感谢的人。

Then taking a boat with His disciples, He crossed the lake to Magdala, at the southern end of the plain of Gennesaret. In the border of Tyre and Sidon His spirit had been refreshed by the confiding trust of the Syrophoenician woman. The heathen people of Decapolis had received Him with gladness. Now as He landed once more in Galilee, where His power had been most strikingly manifested, where most of His works of mercy had been performed, and His teaching given, He was met with contemptuous unbelief.
隨後耶穌和門徒上船渡海，來到革尼撒勒平原南邊馬加丹的境界。在推羅西頓的邊境，耶穌曾因敘利非尼基婦人堅固的信心而精神上甚為愉快。低加波利的異教徒也曾欣然接待祂。現在祂又來到加利利，這是祂的權能表現得最驚人，憐愛的作為和真理的教訓發揮得最多的地方。但祂所遭遇的卻是輕蔑不信。
随后耶稣和门徒上船渡海，来到革尼撒勒平原南边马加丹的境界。在推罗西顿的边境，耶稣曾因叙利非尼基妇人坚固的信心而精神上甚为愉快。低加波利的异教徒也曾欣然接待祂。现在祂又来到加利利，这是祂的权能表现得最惊人，怜爱的作为和真理的教训发挥得最多的地方。但祂所遭遇的却是轻蔑不信。

A deputation of Pharisees had been joined by representatives from the rich and lordly Sadducees, the party of the priests, the skeptics and aristocracy of the nation. The two sects had been at bitter enmity. The Sadducees courted the favor of the ruling power in order to maintain their own position and authority. The Pharisees, on the other hand, fostered the popular hatred against the Romans, longing for the time when they could throw off the yoke of the conqueror. But Pharisee and Sadducee now united against Christ. Like seeks like; and evil, wherever it exists, leagues with evil for the destruction of the good.
這時有一個法利賽人的代表團，會同富貴的撒都該人所委派的代表來見耶穌。撒都該人是猶太國的祭司、懷疑派和貴族所組成的政黨。法利賽人和撒都該人之間有不共戴天之仇。撒都該人一味地討好當時的羅馬政權，藉以保持自己的地位和勢力。法利賽人則慫恿群眾怨恨羅馬，希望有一天能掙脫他們的重軛。但如今法利賽人和撒都該人，卻聯合起來反對基督。這誠然是物以類聚。無論何處，邪惡總是與邪惡結盟，企圖毀滅良善的。
这时有一个法利赛人的代表团，会同富贵的撒都该人所委派的代表来见耶稣。撒都该人是犹太国的祭司、怀疑派和贵族所组成的政党。法利赛人和撒都该人之间有不共戴天之仇。撒都该人一味地讨好当时的罗马政权，借以保持自己的地位和势力。法利赛人则怂恿群众怨恨罗马，希望有一天能挣脱他们的重轭。但如今法利赛人和撒都该人，却联合起来反对基督。这诚然是物以类聚。无论何处，邪恶总是与邪恶结盟，企图毁灭良善的。

Now the Pharisees and Sadducees came to Christ, asking for a sign from heaven. When in the days of Joshua Israel went out to battle with the Canaanites at Bethhoron, the sun had stood still at the leader’s command until victory was gained; and many similar wonders had been manifest in their history. Some such sign was demanded of Jesus. But these signs were not what the Jews needed. No mere external evidence could benefit them. What they needed was not intellectual enlightenment, but spiritual renovation.
這次法利賽人和撒都該人來見基督，要求祂從天上顯個神蹟。在約書亞的時代，以色列人與迦南人在伯和侖作戰的時候，太陽曾聽從以色列首領的命令，在空中停住，直到他們得了勝利。他們的歷史上還記載著許多類似的神蹟。他們向耶穌所要求的，就是這一類的神蹟。但是猶太人實際上所需要的卻不是這些神蹟。僅限外表的憑據不能幫助他們。他們所需要的，不是理智的開導，而是屬靈的更新。
这次法利赛人和撒都该人来见基督，要求祂从天上显个神迹。在约书亚的时代，以色列人与迦南人在伯和仑作战的时候，太阳曾听从以色列首领的命令，在空中停住，直到他们得了胜利。他们的历史上还记载着许多类似的神迹。他们向耶稣所要求的，就是这一类的神迹。但是犹太人实际上所需要的却不是这些神迹。仅限外表的凭据不能帮助他们。他们所需要的，不是理智的开导，而是属灵的更新。

“O ye hypocrites,” said Jesus, “ye can discern the face of the sky,”—by studying the sky they could foretell the weather,—“but can ye not discern the signs of the times?” Christ’s own words, spoken with the power of the Holy Spirit that convicted them of sin, were the sign that God had given for their salvation. And signs direct from heaven had been given to attest the mission of Christ. The song of the angels to the shepherds, the star that guided the wise men, the dove and the voice from heaven at His baptism, were witnesses for Him.
耶穌說：“假冒為善的人那！”“你們知道分辨天上的氣色，”——觀察氣象，預知晴雨──“倒不能分辨這時候的神蹟。”基督親口所講的話，帶著聖靈叫人自覺有罪的能力，就是上帝為拯救他們而顯的神蹟。況且天上也曾直接顯出神蹟為基督的使命作證。牧羊人所聽見天使的歌聲，引領博士們的星光，以及耶穌受浸時從天上降下來的鴿子和聲音，都是為耶穌作見證的。
耶稣说：“假冒为善的人那！”“你们知道分辨天上的气色，”——观察气象，预知晴雨──“倒不能分辨这时候的神迹。”基督亲口所讲的话，带着圣灵叫人自觉有罪的能力，就是上帝为拯救他们而显的神迹。况且天上也曾直接显出神迹为基督的使命作证。牧羊人所听见天使的歌声，引领博士们的星光，以及耶稣受浸时从天上降下来的鸽子和声音，都是为耶稣作见证的。

“And He sighed deeply in His spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign?” “There shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas.” As Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, Christ was to be the same time “in the heart of the earth.” And as the preaching of Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so Christ’s preaching was a sign to His generation. But what a contrast in the reception of the word! The people of the great heathen city trembled as they heard the warning from God. Kings and nobles humbled themselves; the high and the lowly together cried to the God of heaven, and His mercy was granted unto them. “The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation,” Christ had said, “and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.” Matthew 12:40, 41.

“耶穌心裡深深的嘆息說，這世代為什麼求神蹟呢？”“除了先知約拿的神蹟以外，再沒有神蹟給他們看！”“約拿三日三夜在大魚肚腹中，人子也要這樣三日三夜在地裡頭”（太12:39,40）。約拿所傳的道，是向尼尼微人所顯的神蹟。照樣，基督所傳的道，也是向當祂的世代所顯的神蹟。然而兩個世代對於所傳給他們的道，有何等不同的反應啊！那異邦大城裡的居民聽見上帝的警告，無不膽戰心驚。君王和大臣都披麻蒙灰，禁食禱告，全城的人無論貧富貴賤都向天上的上帝呼求。上帝就向他們施恩。基督曾說：“當審判的時候，尼尼微人，要起來定這世代的罪，因為尼尼微人聽了約拿所傳的，就悔改了，看哪，在這裡有一人比約拿更大”（太12:41）。

“耶稣心里深深的叹息说，这世代为什么求神迹呢？”“除了先知约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看！”“约拿三日三夜在大鱼肚腹中，人子也要这样三日三夜在地里头”（太12:39,40）。约拿所传的道，是向尼尼微人所显的神迹。照样，基督所传的道，也是向当祂的世代所显的神迹。然而两个世代对于所传给他们的道，有何等不同的反应啊！那异邦大城里的居民听见上帝的警告，无不胆战心惊。君王和大臣都披麻蒙灰，禁食祷告，全城的人无论贫富贵贱都向天上的上帝呼求。上帝就向他们施恩。基督曾说：“当审判的时候，尼尼微人，要起来定这世代的罪，因为尼尼微人听了约拿所传的，就悔改了，看哪，在这里有一人比约拿更大”（太12:41）。

Every miracle that Christ performed was a sign of His divinity. He was doing the very work that had been foretold of the Messiah; but to the Pharisees these works of mercy were a positive offense. The Jewish leaders looked with heartless indifference on human suffering. In many cases their selfishness and oppression had caused the affliction that Christ relieved. Thus His miracles were to them a reproach.
基督所行的每一件神蹟，都是祂神性的表徵。祂所做的正是聖經預言彌賽亞所要做的事。但在法利賽人看來，這些慈憐的作為卻是他們的絆腳石。猶太人的領袖們對於人類的痛苦冷酷無情，漠不關心。基督所解除的許多痛苦，事實上是法利賽人的自私和壓迫所造成的。因此祂所行的神蹟對於他們是一種譴責。
基督所行的每一件神迹，都是祂神性的表征。祂所做的正是圣经预言弥赛亚所要做的事。但在法利赛人看来，这些慈怜的作为却是他们的绊脚石。犹太人的领袖们对于人类的痛苦冷酷无情，漠不关心。基督所解除的许多痛苦，事实上是法利赛人的自私和压迫所造成的。因此祂所行的神迹对于他们是一种谴责。

That which led the Jews to reject the Saviour’s work was the highest evidence of His divine character. The greatest significance of His miracles is seen in the fact that they were for the blessing of humanity. The highest evidence that He came from God is that His life revealed the character of God. He did the works and spoke the words of God. Such a life is the greatest of all miracles.
那使猶太人拒絕救主工做的事，正是祂神性的最大憑據。祂的神蹟所含最大意義可以從為人類造福的事實上看出來。祂的生活彰顯了上帝的品德，這就是最確鑿的憑據，證明祂是從上帝那裡來的。祂作上帝的工，說上帝的話。這種人生是一切神蹟中最大的神蹟。
那使犹太人拒绝救主工做的事，正是祂神性的最大凭据。祂的神迹所含最大意义可以从为人类造福的事实上看出来。祂的生活彰显了上帝的品德，这就是最确凿的凭据，证明祂是从上帝那里来的。祂作上帝的工，说上帝的话。这种人生是一切神迹中最大的神迹。

When the message of truth is presented in our day, there are many who, like the Jews, cry, Show us a sign. Work us a miracle. Christ wrought no miracle at the demand of the Pharisees. He wrought no miracle in the wilderness in answer to Satan’s insinuations. He does not impart to us power to vindicate ourselves or to satisfy the demands of unbelief and pride. But the gospel is not without a sign of its divine origin. Is it not a miracle that we can break from the bondage of Satan? Enmity against Satan is not natural to the human heart; it is implanted by the grace of God. When one who has been controlled by a stubborn, wayward will is set free, and yields himself wholeheartedly to the drawing of God’s heavenly agencies, a miracle is wrought; so also when a man who has been under strong delusion comes to understand moral truth. Every time a soul is converted, and learns to love God and keep His commandments, the promise of God is fulfilled, “A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.” Ezekiel 36:26. The change in human hearts, the transformation of human characters, is a miracle that reveals an ever-living Saviour, working to rescue souls. A consistent life in Christ is a great miracle. In the preaching of the word of God, the sign that should be manifest now and always is the presence of the Holy Spirit, to make the word a regenerating power to those that hear. This is God’s witness before the world to the divine mission of His Son.

當真理的資訊傳給現今的世代時，許多人也像猶太人一樣說：顯一個神蹟，行一件奇事給我們看。基督沒有因法利賽人的要求而行什麼奇事。祂在曠野也沒有行一個神蹟來答覆撒但的巧言。祂並不賜給我們能力來表揚自己，或滿足不信和驕傲之人的要求。但福音並不是沒有表徵來證明它是出於上帝的。我們能掙脫撒但的捆綁，豈不是一件神蹟嗎？與撒但為仇，原不是人的本性，乃是上帝的恩典所賦予的。每當一個被倔強放蕩的意志所轄制的人得到自由，而全心全意地順從上帝能力的引領時，這就是一個神蹟。每當一個在強烈的迷惑之下的人幡然覺悟，明白真道，這也是一個神蹟。每逢一個人悔改，敬愛上帝並遵守祂的誡命，上帝以下的應許就實現在他身上：“我也要賜給你們一個新心，將新靈放在你們裡面”（結36:26）。人心的更新，品格的變化，都是神蹟，顯明一位永活的救主在為拯救生靈而工作。在基督裡言行一致的人生是一個偉大的神蹟。人傳講上帝的道時所應當一貫表顯的神蹟，就是聖靈的同在，使上帝的道在聽眾身上發揮重生的能力。這是上帝向全世界為祂兒子的神聖使命所做的見證。

当真理的信息传给现今的世代时，许多人也像犹太人一样说：显一个神迹，行一件奇事给我们看。基督没有因法利赛人的要求而行什么奇事。祂在旷野也没有行一个神迹来答复撒但的巧言。祂并不赐给我们能力来表扬自己，或满足不信和骄傲之人的要求。但福音并不是没有表征来证明它是出于上帝的。我们能挣脱撒但的捆绑，岂不是一件神迹吗？与撒但为仇，原不是人的本性，乃是上帝的恩典所赋予的。每当一个被倔强放荡的意志所辖制的人得到自由，而全心全意地顺从上帝能力的引领时，这就是一个神迹。每当一个在强烈的迷惑之下的人幡然觉悟，明白真道，这也是一个神迹。每逢一个人悔改，敬爱上帝并遵守祂的诫命，上帝以下的应许就实现在他身上：“我也要赐给你们一个新心，将新灵放在你们里面”（结36:26）。人心的更新，品格的变化，都是神迹，显明一位永活的救主在为拯救生灵而工作。在基督里言行一致的人生是一个伟大的神迹。人传讲上帝的道时所应当一贯表显的神迹，就是圣灵的同在，使上帝的道在听众身上发挥重生的能力。这是上帝向全世界为祂儿子的神圣使命所做的见证。

Those who desired a sign from Jesus had so hardened their hearts in unbelief that they did not discern in His character the likeness of God. They would not see that His mission was in fulfillment of the Scriptures. In the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, Jesus said to the Pharisees, “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.” Luke 16:31. No sign that could be given in heaven or earth would benefit them.
那些向耶穌求神蹟的人已經因不信而心地剛硬，以致不能在耶穌的品格上看出上帝的形像。他們不願明白耶穌的使命是應驗了聖經。耶穌用財主和拉撒路的比喻對法利賽人說：“若不聽從摩西和先知的話，就是有一個從死裡復活的，他們也是不聽勸”（路16: 31）。在天上地上所能顯的任何神蹟都不能幫助他們。
那些向耶稣求神迹的人已经因不信而心地刚硬，以致不能在耶稣的品格上看出上帝的形像。他们不愿明白耶稣的使命是应验了圣经。耶稣用财主和拉撒路的比喻对法利赛人说：“若不听从摩西和先知的话，就是有一个从死里复活的，他们也是不听劝”（路16: 31）。在天上地上所能显的任何神迹都不能帮助他们。

Jesus “sighed deeply in His spirit,” and, turning from the group of cavilers, re-entered the boat with His disciples. In sorrowful silence they again crossed the lake. They did not, however, return to the place they had left, but directed their course toward Bethsaida, near where the five thousand had been fed. Upon reaching the farther side, Jesus said, “Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” The Jews had been accustomed since the days of Moses to put away leaven from their houses at the Passover season, and they had thus been taught to regard it as a type of sin. Yet the disciples failed to understand Jesus. In their sudden departure from Magdala they had forgotten to take bread, and they had with them only one loaf. To this circumstance they understood Christ to refer, warning them not to buy bread of a Pharisee or a Sadducee. Their lack of faith and spiritual insight had often led them to similar misconception of His words. Now Jesus reproved them for thinking that He who had fed thousands with a few fishes and barley loaves could in that solemn warning have referred merely to temporal food. There was danger that the crafty reasoning of the Pharisees and the Sadducees would leaven His disciples with unbelief, causing them to think lightly of the works of Christ.

耶穌“深深地嘆息”，就離開這一群吹毛求疵的人，同門徒再上船，在憂鬱的靜默中渡海。他們沒有回到以前離開的地方，而往伯賽大，靠近耶穌給五千人吃飽的地方去。到了彼岸，耶穌就對門徒說：“你們要謹慎，防備法利賽人和撒都該人的酵。”從摩西的時候起，猶太人每逢過逾越節，必須除去家中的面酵。他們把酵看為罪惡的表號。可是門徒不瞭解耶穌的意思。他們匆匆離開馬加丹，忘記帶餅，所以船上只剩了一個餅。他們以為耶穌所講的是指著這一件事，是警戒他們不要向法利賽人和撒都該人買餅。這些門徒缺乏信心和屬靈的見識，所以對於救主的話常發生這樣的誤會。如今耶穌責備他們，不該認為祂這能用幾條魚和幾個餅給成千人吃飽的主，會在這嚴肅的警告中僅僅論到肉體的食物。耶穌所見到的危險，是法利賽人和撒都該人那種狡猾的論辯，將有面酵的作用，在門徒心中引起不信，使他們輕看基督的工作。

耶稣“深深地叹息”，就离开这一群吹毛求疵的人，同门徒再上船，在忧郁的静默中渡海。他们没有回到以前离开的地方，而往伯赛大，靠近耶稣给五千人吃饱的地方去。到了彼岸，耶稣就对门徒说：“你们要谨慎，防备法利赛人和撒都该人的酵。”从摩西的时候起，犹太人每逢过逾越节，必须除去家中的面酵。他们把酵看为罪恶的表号。可是门徒不了解耶稣的意思。他们匆匆离开马加丹，忘记带饼，所以船上只剩了一个饼。他们以为耶稣所讲的是指着这一件事，是警戒他们不要向法利赛人和撒都该人买饼。这些门徒缺乏信心和属灵的见识，所以对于救主的话常发生这样的误会。如今耶稣责备他们，不该认为祂这能用几条鱼和几个饼给成千人吃饱的主，会在这严肃的警告中仅仅论到肉体的食物。耶稣所见到的危险，是法利赛人和撒都该人那种狡猾的论辩，将有面酵的作用，在门徒心中引起不信，使他们轻看基督的工作。

The disciples were inclined to think that their Master should have granted the demand for a sign in the heavens. They believed that He was fully able to do this, and that such a sign would put His enemies to silence. They did not discern the hypocrisy of these cavilers.
門徒認為他們的夫子應當答應這班人的要求，從天上顯個神蹟。他們深信祂很可以作到這一件事，而且這樣的一個神蹟，必能使祂的仇敵啞口無言。但他們沒有看透那些無理強辯者的虛偽。
门徒认为他们的夫子应当答应这班人的要求，从天上显个神迹。他们深信祂很可以作到这一件事，而且这样的一个神迹，必能使祂的仇敌哑口无言。但他们没有看透那些无理强辩者的虚伪。

Months afterward, “when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another,” Jesus repeated the same teaching. “He began to say unto His disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” Luke 12:1.
過了幾個月，某一天，“有幾萬人聚集，甚至彼此踐踏。”耶穌又講了這話。祂“開講，先對門徒說：你們要防備法利賽人的酵，就是假冒為善”（路12:1）。
过了几个月，某一天，“有几万人聚集，甚至彼此践踏。”耶稣又讲了这话。祂“开讲，先对门徒说：你们要防备法利赛人的酵，就是假冒为善”（路12:1）。

The leaven placed in the meal works imperceptibly, changing the whole mass to its own nature. So if hypocrisy is allowed to exist in the heart, it permeates the character and the life. A striking example of the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, Christ had already rebuked in denouncing the practice of “Corban,” by which a neglect of filial duty was concealed under a pretense of liberality to the temple. The scribes and Pharisees were insinuating deceptive principles. They concealed the real tendency of their doctrines, and improved every occasion to instill them artfully into the minds of their hearers. These false principles, when once accepted, worked like leaven in the meal, permeating and transforming the character. It was this deceptive teaching that made it so hard for the people to receive the words of Christ.

Peter declared, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” He waited not for kingly honors to crown his Lord, but accepted Him in His humiliation.

彼得從起初就相信耶穌是彌賽亞。許多其他信服施洗約翰的資訊而接受基督的人，在約翰下監和被殺時，就開始懷疑約翰的使命了。這些人現在又懷疑耶穌是他們所長久仰望的彌賽亞。還有許多曾經熱烈盼望耶穌登上大衛寶座的門徒，後來發現祂沒有這種打算，就離開了祂。但彼得和他的同伴並沒有改變他們對耶穌的忠誠。那些昨天稱讚耶穌而今日毀謗祂的人所有朝三暮四的行為，並沒有影響救主真誠門徒的信心。彼得說：“你是基督，是永生上帝的兒子。”他沒有等待君王的尊榮加在他主的頭上，而就在祂的屈辱中承認了祂。

彼得从起初就相信耶稣是弥赛亚。许多其他信服施洗约翰的信息而接受基督的人，在约翰下监和被杀时，就开始怀疑约翰的使命了。这些人现在又怀疑耶稣是他们所长久仰望的弥赛亚。还有许多曾经热烈盼望耶稣登上大卫宝座的门徒，后来发现祂没有这种打算，就离开了祂。但彼得和他的同伴并没有改变他们对耶稣的忠诚。那些昨天称赞耶稣而今日毁谤祂的人所有朝三暮四的行为，并没有影响救主真诚门徒的信心。彼得说：“你是基督，是永生上帝的儿子。”他没有等待君王的尊荣加在他主的头上，而就在祂的屈辱中承认了祂。

Peter had expressed the faith of the twelve. Yet the disciples were still far from understanding Christ’s mission. The opposition and misrepresentation of the priests and rulers, while it could not turn them away from Christ, still caused them great perplexity. They did not see their way clearly. The influence of their early training, the teaching of the rabbis, the power of tradition, still intercepted their view of truth. From time to time precious rays of light from Jesus shone upon them, yet often they were like men groping among shadows. But on this day, before they were brought face to face with the great trial of their faith, the Holy Spirit rested upon them in power. For a little time their eyes were turned away from “the things which are seen,” to behold “the things which are not seen.” 2 Corinthians 4:18. Beneath the guise of humanity they discerned the glory of the Son of God.

彼得所表白的是十二門徒的信心。但他們對於基督使命的認識還是很膚淺的。祭司和官長的反對和曲解，雖不能使他們離開基督，但總不免使他們大為困惑。他們還有許多不能明白的事。他們幼年所受教育的影響和拉比們的教訓，以及遺傳的力量，仍模糊了他們對於真理的認識。從耶穌身上放出來的光亮，時時照耀著他們，然而他們往往仍像在黑暗中摸索著的人。但這一天，在他們面臨信心的大考驗之前，聖靈的能力降在他們身上。他們的眼睛在一時之間從“所見的”事，轉到“所不見的”事上（林後4:18）。在人性的外表之下，他們認出了上帝兒子的榮耀。

彼得所表白的是十二门徒的信心。但他们对于基督使命的认识还是很肤浅的。祭司和官长的反对和曲解，虽不能使他们离开基督，但总不免使他们大为困惑。他们还有许多不能明白的事。他们幼年所受教育的影响和拉比们的教训，以及遗传的力量，仍模糊了他们对于真理的认识。从耶稣身上放出来的光亮，时时照耀着他们，然而他们往往仍像在黑暗中摸索着的人。但这一天，在他们面临信心的大考验之前，圣灵的能力降在他们身上。他们的眼睛在一时之间从“所见的”事，转到“所不见的”事上（林后4:18）。在人性的外表之下，他们认出了上帝儿子的荣耀。
Jesus answered Peter, saying, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but My Father which is in heaven.”
耶穌回答彼得說：“西門巴約拿，你是有福的，因為這不是屬血肉的指示你的，乃是我在天上的父指示的。”
耶稣回答彼得说：“西门巴约拿，你是有福的，因为这不是属血肉的指示你的，乃是我在天上的父指示的。”

The truth which Peter had confessed is the foundation of the believer’s faith. It is that which Christ Himself has declared to be eternal life. But the possession of this knowledge was no ground for self-glorification. Through no wisdom or goodness of his own had it been revealed to Peter. Never can humanity, of itself, attain to a knowledge of the divine. “It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?” Job 11:8. Only the spirit of adoption can reveal to us the deep things of God, which “eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man.” “God hath revealed them unto us by His Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” 1 Corinthians 2:9, 10. “The secret of the Lord is with them that fear Him;” and the fact that Peter discerned the glory of Christ was an evidence that he had been “taught of God.” Psalm 25:14; John 6:45. Ah, indeed, “blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee.”

彼得所承認的真理是信徒信心的基礎。這就是基督親自所宣佈為永生的真理。但人雖有這種知識，卻不可因而自豪。彼得得到這個啟示，並不是因為他自己有什麼智慧或良善行。人類靠自己永不能認識上帝。“祂的智慧高於天，你還能做什麼？深於陰間，你還能知道什麼”（伯11:8）？只有那使我們得到兒子名分的靈，才能將上帝深奧的事啟示我們，就是“眼睛未曾看見，耳朵未曾聽見，人心也未曾想到的。”“上帝藉著聖靈向我們顯明瞭，因為聖靈參透萬事，就是上帝深奧的事也參透了”（林前2:9,10）。“耶和華與敬畏祂的人親密，祂必將自己的約指示他們”（詩25:14）。彼得既能認識基督的榮耀，就證明他已“蒙上帝的教訓”（約6:45）。的確，“西門巴約拿，你是有福的，因為這不是屬血肉的指示你的，乃是我在天上的父指示的。”

彼得所承认的真理是信徒信心的基础。这就是基督亲自所宣布为永生的真理。但人虽有这种知识，却不可因而自豪。彼得得到这个启示，并不是因为他自己有什么智慧或良善行。人类靠自己永不能认识上帝。“祂的智慧高于天，你还能做什么？深于阴间，你还能知道什么”（伯11:8）？只有那使我们得到儿子名分的灵，才能将上帝深奥的事启示我们，就是“眼睛未曾看见，耳朵未曾听见，人心也未曾想到的。”“上帝借着圣灵向我们显明了，因为圣灵参透万事，就是上帝深奥的事也参透了”（林前2:9,10）。“耶和华与敬畏祂的人亲密，祂必将自己的约指示他们”（诗25:14）。彼得既能认识基督的荣耀，就证明他已“蒙上帝的教训”（约6:45）。的确，“西门巴约拿，你是有福的，因为这不是属血肉的指示你的，乃是我在天上的父指示的。”

Jesus continued: “I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” The word Peter signifies a stone,—a rolling stone. Peter was not the rock upon which the church was founded. The gates of hell did prevail against him when he denied his Lord with cursing and swearing. The church was built upon One against whom the gates of hell could not prevail.
耶穌接著說：“我還告訴你，你是彼得，我要把我的教會建造在這磐石上，陰間的權柄，不能勝過他”“彼得”就是石頭的意思──一塊活動的石頭。彼得並不是那有教會建立在其上的磐石。在他發咒起誓不承認主的時候，陰間的權柄確已勝過了他。教會乃是要建立在一位陰間的權柄所不能勝過的主身上。
耶稣接着说：“我还告诉你，你是彼得，我要把我的教会建造在这磐石上，阴间的权柄，不能胜过他”“彼得”就是石头的意思──一块活动的石头。彼得并不是那有教会建立在其上的磐石。在他发咒起誓不承认主的时候，阴间的权柄确已胜过了他。教会乃是要建立在一位阴间的权柄所不能胜过的主身上。

Centuries before the Saviour’s advent Moses had pointed to the Rock of Israel’s salvation. The psalmist had sung of “the Rock of my strength.” Isaiah had written, “Thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation.” Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 62:7; Isaiah 28:16. Peter himself, writing by inspiration, applies this prophecy to Jesus. He says, “If ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious: unto whom coming, a living stone, rejected indeed of men, but with God elect, precious, ye also, as living stones, are built up a spiritual house.” 1 Peter 2:3-5, R. V.

在救主降世之前一千多年，摩西曾指出以色列救恩的磐石。詩人大衛曾歌頌“我力量的磐石。”以賽亞也曾寫道：“所以主耶和華如此說，看那！我在錫安放一塊石頭，作為根基，是試驗過的石頭，是穩固根基，寶貴的房角石”（申32:4；詩62:7；賽28:16）。彼得自己也曾受聖靈的感動引用這段預言來指著耶穌說：“你們若嘗過主恩的滋味，就必如此。主乃活石，固然是被人所棄的，卻是被上帝所揀選所寶貴的。你們來到主面前，也就像活石，被建造成為靈宮”（彼前2:3-5）。

在救主降世之前一千多年，摩西曾指出以色列救恩的磐石。诗人大卫曾歌颂“我力量的磐石。”以赛亚也曾写道：“所以主耶和华如此说，看那！我在锡安放一块石头，作为根基，是试验过的石头，是稳固根基，宝贵的房角石”（申32:4；诗62:7；赛28:16）。彼得自己也曾受圣灵的感动引用这段预言来指着耶稣说：“你们若尝过主恩的滋味，就必如此。主乃活石，固然是被人所弃的，却是被上帝所拣选所宝贵的。你们来到主面前，也就像活石，被建造成为灵宫”（彼前2:3-5）。

“Other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” 1 Corinthians 3:11. “Upon this rock,” said Jesus, “I will build My church.” In the presence of God, and all the heavenly intelligences, in the presence of the unseen army of hell, Christ founded His church upon the living Rock. That Rock is Himself,— His own body, for us broken and bruised. Against the church built upon this foundation, the gates of hell shall not prevail.
“因為那已經立好的根基，就是耶穌基督，此外沒有人能立別的根基”（林前3:11）。耶穌說：“我要把我的教會建造在這磐石上。”基督在上帝和天上一切眾生，以及陰間看不見的眾軍面前，將祂的教會建造在活的磐石上。那磐石就是祂自己——祂自己的身體，曾為我們捨棄而壓傷的身體。建造在這個根基上的教會，是陰間的權柄所不能勝過的。
“因为那已经立好的根基，就是耶稣基督，此外没有人能立别的根基”（林前3:11）。耶稣说：“我要把我的教会建造在这磐石上。”基督在上帝和天上一切众生，以及阴间看不见的众军面前，将祂的教会建造在活的磐石上。那磐石就是祂自己——祂自己的身体，曾为我们舍弃而压伤的身体。建造在这个根基上的教会，是阴间的权柄所不能胜过的。

How feeble the church appeared when Christ spoke these words! There was only a handful of believers, against whom all the power of demons and evil men would be directed; yet the followers of Christ were not to fear. Built upon the Rock of their strength, they could not be overthrown.
基督說這些話的時候，當日的教會顯得多麼脆弱啊！那時信徒寥寥無幾，並有魔鬼和惡人的一切勢力向他們猛烈襲擊。但基督的門徒不必懼怕。他們是建造在他們力量的磐石上，是不能被推翻的。
基督说这些话的时候，当日的教会显得多么脆弱啊！那时信徒寥寥无几，并有魔鬼和恶人的一切势力向他们猛烈袭击。但基督的门徒不必惧怕。他们是建造在他们力量的磐石上，是不能被推翻的。
For six thousand years, faith has builded upon Christ. For six thousand years the floods and tempests of satanic wrath have beaten upon the Rock of our salvation; but it stands unmoved.
六千年來，上帝子民的信仰，是建立在基督身上的。六千年來，撒但忿怒的狂濤和風暴不住地衝撞我們救恩的磐石，但這磐石仍然屹立，毫不動搖。
六千年来，上帝子民的信仰，是建立在基督身上的。六千年来，撒但忿怒的狂涛和风暴不住地冲撞我们救恩的磐石，但这磐石仍然屹立，毫不动摇。

Peter had expressed the truth which is the foundation of the church’s faith, and Jesus now honored him as the representative of the whole body of believers. He said, “I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.”
彼得已經說明了那作為教會信仰根基的真理。於是耶穌就尊重他為全體信徒的代表。祂說：“我要把天國的鑰匙給你，凡你在地上所捆綁的，在天上也要捆綁，凡你在地上所釋放的，在天上也要釋放。”
彼得已经说明了那作为教会信仰根基的真理。于是耶稣就尊重他为全体信徒的代表。祂说：“我要把天国的钥匙给你，凡你在地上所捆绑的，在天上也要捆绑，凡你在地上所释放的，在天上也要释放。”

“The keys of the kingdom of heaven” are the words of Christ. All the words of Holy Scripture are His, and are here included. These words have power to open and to shut heaven. They declare the conditions upon which men are received or rejected. Thus the work of those who preach God’s word is a savor of life unto life or of death unto death. Theirs is a mission weighted with eternal results.
“天國的鑰匙”乃是基督的道。它包括聖經上一切的話。這些話有開啟和關閉天國之門的力量，並宣佈世人被上天接受或拒絕的條件。所以那些宣講上帝之道的人的工作，在得救的人身上，做了活的香氣叫人活，在滅亡的人身上，做了死的香氣叫人死（見林後2:15，16）。門徒的使命，維繫著永恆的結局。
“天国的钥匙”乃是基督的道。它包括圣经上一切的话。这些话有开启和关闭天国之门的力量，并宣布世人被上天接受或拒绝的条件。所以那些宣讲上帝之道的人的工作，在得救的人身上，做了活的香气叫人活，在灭亡的人身上，做了死的香气叫人死（见林后2:15，16）。门徒的使命，维系着永恒的结局。

The Saviour did not commit the work of the gospel to Peter individually. At a later time, repeating the words that were spoken to Peter, He applied them directly to the church. And the same in substance was spoken also to the twelve as representatives of the body of believers. If Jesus had delegated any special authority to one of the disciples above the others, we should not find them so often contending as to who should be the greatest. They would have submitted to the wish of their Master, and honored the one whom He had chosen.
救主並沒有把傳福音的工作委託給彼得一人。後來祂把對彼得所說的話重述了一遍，便是直接對教會說的。祂也曾向代表全體信徒的十二個門徒說過與這相仿的話。如果耶穌曾以任何特殊的權柄，賦予門徒中的一個人，使他位居其他門徒之上，那麼，我們就不致於看到他們再爭論誰為大了。他們必會服從他們夫子的意思，並尊重祂所揀選的人。
救主并没有把传福音的工作委托给彼得一人。后来祂把对彼得所说的话重述了一遍，便是直接对教会说的。祂也曾向代表全体信徒的十二个门徒说过与这相仿的话。如果耶稣曾以任何特殊的权柄，赋予门徒中的一个人，使他位居其他门徒之上，那么，我们就不致于看到他们再争论谁为大了。他们必会服从他们夫子的意思，并尊重祂所拣选的人。
Instead of appointing one to be their head, Christ said to the disciples, “Be not ye called Rabbi;” “neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ.” Matthew 23:8, 10.
基督沒有指定一個人作他們的領袖，只是對他們說：“你們不要受拉比的稱呼，”“也不要受師尊的稱呼，因為只有一位是你們的師尊，就是基督”（太23:8-10）。
基督没有指定一个人作他们的领袖，只是对他们说：“你们不要受拉比的称呼，”“也不要受师尊的称呼，因为只有一位是你们的师尊，就是基督”（太23:8-10）。

“The head of every man is Christ.” God, who put all things under the Saviour’s feet, “gave Him to be the head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of Him that filleth all in all.” 1 Corinthians 11:3; Ephesians 1:22, 23. The church is built upon Christ as its foundation; it is to obey Christ as its head. It is not to depend upon man, or be controlled by man. Many claim that a position of trust in the church gives them authority to dictate what other men shall believe and what they shall do. This claim God does not sanction. The Saviour declares, “All ye are brethren.” All are exposed to temptation, and are liable to error. Upon no finite being can we depend for guidance. The Rock of faith is the living presence of Christ in the church. Upon this the weakest may depend, and those who think themselves the strongest will prove to be the weakest, unless they make Christ their efficiency. “Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm.” The Lord “is the Rock, His work is perfect.” “Blessed are all they that put their trust in Him.” Jeremiah 17:5; Deuteronomy 32:4; Psalm 2:12.

“基督是各人的頭。”那將萬有服在救主腳下的上帝，“使祂為教會作萬有之首，教會是祂的身體，是那充滿萬有者所充滿的”（林前11:3；弗1:22,23）。教會以基督為建造的根基，就當以祂為教會的元首而順從祂。教會不可依賴人，或受人的控制。許多人認為自己在教會里既擔任負責的職位，就有權柄發號施令，告訴別人應當信什麼，做什麼。這種主觀是上帝所不認可的。救主說：“你們都是弟兄。”人人都是撒但誘惑的物件，而且都是容易犯錯誤的。我們不能依賴智慧有限的人作我們的嚮導。信心的磐石，就是在教會中間活著的基督。最軟弱的人儘可以依靠祂，而那些自以為最強壯的人，若不以基督為他們的力量，就必顯為最軟弱的了。“倚靠人血肉的膀臂……那人有禍了”（耶17:5）。耶和華“是磐石，祂的作為完全”（申32:4）。“凡投靠祂的，都是有福的”（詩2:12）。

“基督是各人的头。”那将万有服在救主脚下的上帝，“使祂为教会作万有之首，教会是祂的身体，是那充满万有者所充满的”（林前11:3；弗1:22,23）。教会以基督为建造的根基，就当以祂为教会的元首而顺从祂。教会不可依赖人，或受人的控制。许多人认为自己在教会里既担任负责的职位，就有权柄发号施令，告诉别人应当信什么，做什么。这种主观是上帝所不认可的。救主说：“你们都是弟兄。”人人都是撒但诱惑的对象，而且都是容易犯错误的。我们不能依赖智能有限的人作我们的向导。信心的磐石，就是在教会中间活着的基督。最软弱的人尽可以依靠祂，而那些自以为最强壮的人，若不以基督为他们的力量，就必显为最软弱的了。“倚靠人血肉的膀臂……那人有祸了”（耶17:5）。耶和华“是磐石，祂的作为完全”（申32:4）。“凡投靠祂的，都是有福的”（诗2:12）。

After Peter’s confession, Jesus charged the disciples to tell no man that He was the Christ. This charge was given because of the determined opposition of the scribes and Pharisees. More than this, the people, and even the disciples, had so false a conception of the Messiah that a public announcement of Him would give them no true idea of His character or His work. But day by day He was revealing Himself to them as the Saviour, and thus He desired to give them a true conception of Him as the Messiah.
在彼得承認基督之後，耶穌囑咐門徒不要告訴人祂是基督。祂這樣囑咐他們，是因為有文士和法利賽人在堅決地反對祂。再者，眾人──連門徒在內，對於彌賽亞的觀念是那麼模糊，以致公開地宣佈祂為彌賽亞，並不能使他們對於祂的身份或工作有真正的認識。所以祂還要天天向他們顯示自己是救主，希望這樣做，就可以使他們對祂彌賽亞的身份有正確的觀念。
在彼得承认基督之后，耶稣嘱咐门徒不要告诉人祂是基督。祂这样嘱咐他们，是因为有文士和法利赛人在坚决地反对祂。再者，众人──连门徒在内，对于弥赛亚的观念是那么模糊，以致公开地宣布祂为弥赛亚，并不能使他们对于祂的身份或工作有真正的认识。所以祂还要天天向他们显示自己是救主，希望这样做，就可以使他们对祂弥赛亚的身份有正确的观念。

The disciples still expected Christ to reign as a temporal prince. Although He had so long concealed His design, they believed that He would not always remain in poverty and obscurity; the time was near when He would establish His kingdom. That the hatred of the priests and rabbis would never be overcome, that Christ would be rejected by His own nation, condemned as a deceiver, and crucified as a malefactor,—such a thought the disciples had never entertained. But the hour of the power of darkness was drawing on, and Jesus must open to His disciples the conflict before them. He was sad as He anticipated the trial.
門徒仍希望基督在世上作王。雖然基督這樣長久沒有發表自己的計劃，他們還是相信祂絕不會長此窮困，湮沒無聞。他們總以為祂立國的時候已經近了。若是說祭司和拉比們的仇恨永遠不會打消，基督將為本國的人所拒絕，像騙子那樣被定死罪，像惡人一樣被釘十字架上──門徒從來沒有這樣想過。但黑暗掌權的時候近了。耶穌必須把門徒面臨的鬥爭告訴他們。祂想到這行將臨到的試煉，就憂愁起來。
门徒仍希望基督在世上作王。虽然基督这样长久没有发表自己的计划，他们还是相信祂绝不会长此穷困，湮没无闻。他们总以为祂立国的时候已经近了。若是说祭司和拉比们的仇恨永远不会打消，基督将为本国的人所拒绝，像骗子那样被定死罪，像恶人一样被钉十字架上──门徒从来没有这样想过。但黑暗掌权的时候近了。耶稣必须把门徒面临的斗争告诉他们。祂想到这行将临到的试炼，就忧愁起来。

Hitherto He had refrained from making known to them anything relative to His sufferings and death. In His conversation with Nicodemus He had said, “As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have eternal life.” John 3:14, 15. But the disciples did not hear this, and had they heard, would not have understood. But now they have been with Jesus, listening to His words, beholding His works, until, notwithstanding the humility of His surroundings, and the opposition of priests and people, they can join in the testimony of Peter, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Now the time has come for the veil that hides the future to be withdrawn. “From that time forth began Jesus to show unto His disciples, how that He must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.”

直到如今，祂還沒有把任何有關自己受苦受死的事告訴門徒。祂和尼哥底母談話時曾這樣說：“摩西在曠野怎樣舉蛇，人子也必照樣被舉起來，叫一切信祂的都得永生”（約3:14,15）。可是門徒沒有聽見過這話，就是聽見了也不會明白的。但現在他們已與耶穌相處很久，聽見祂的教訓，看見祂的作為。耶穌的境遇雖然低微，且遭祭司和眾人的反對，他們仍能與彼得同聲承認說：“你是基督，是永生上帝的兒子。”現在的時機已經成熟，那遮著未來之事的幔子必須揭開了。“從此耶穌才指示門徒，祂必須上耶路撒冷去，受長老、祭司長、文士許多的苦，並且被殺，第三日復活。”

直到如今，祂还没有把任何有关自己受苦受死的事告诉门徒。祂和尼哥底母谈话时曾这样说：“摩西在旷野怎样举蛇，人子也必照样被举起来，叫一切信祂的都得永生”（约3:14,15）。可是门徒没有听见过这话，就是听见了也不会明白的。但现在他们已与耶稣相处很久，听见祂的教训，看见祂的作为。耶稣的境遇虽然低微，且遭祭司和众人的反对，他们仍能与彼得同声承认说：“你是基督，是永生上帝的儿子。”现在的时机已经成熟，那遮着未来之事的幔子必须揭开了。“从此耶稣才指示门徒，祂必须上耶路撒冷去，受长老、祭司长、文士许多的苦，并且被杀，第三日复活。”

Speechless with grief and amazement, the disciples listened. Christ had accepted Peter’s acknowledgment of Him as the Son of God; and now His words pointing to His suffering and death seemed incomprehensible. Peter could not keep silent. He laid hold upon his Master, as if to draw Him back from His impending doom, exclaiming, “Be it far from Thee, Lord: this shall not be unto Thee.”
門徒聽了這話，一言不發，既感驚異，又覺憂愁。基督已經接受彼得承認祂是上帝的兒子，現在祂指著自己受苦受死的話，似乎令人難解。彼得不能保持緘默了。他拉住他的夫子，好像要把祂從面臨的厄運中拉回來，喊著說：“主啊！萬不可如此，這事必不臨到你身上。”
门徒听了这话，一言不发，既感惊异，又觉忧愁。基督已经接受彼得承认祂是上帝的儿子，现在祂指着自己受苦受死的话，似乎令人难解。彼得不能保持缄默了。他拉住他的夫子，好像要把祂从面临的厄运中拉回来，喊着说：“主啊！万不可如此，这事必不临到你身上。”

Peter loved his Lord; but Jesus did not commend him for thus manifesting the desire to shield Him from suffering. Peter’s words were not such as would be a help and solace to Jesus in the great trial before Him. They were not in harmony with God’s purpose of grace toward a lost world, nor with the lesson of self-sacrifice that Jesus had come to teach by His own example. Peter did not desire to see the cross in the work of Christ. The impression which his words would make was directly opposed to that which Christ desired to make on the minds of His followers, and the Saviour was moved to utter one of the sternest rebukes that ever fell from His lips: “Get thee behind Me, Satan: thou art an offense unto Me: for thou savorest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.”

彼得熱愛他的主，但是耶穌沒有因彼得這樣表示渴望保護祂脫離苦難而稱讚他。彼得的話，在耶穌面臨的大試煉中，並不足以使祂得到幫助和安慰。這些話並不符合上帝對於失喪世界所有恩典的旨意，也不符合耶穌來用自己的榜樣所發揮自我犧牲的教訓。彼得不願意在基督的工作上看到一個十字架。彼得這些話所造成的印象，與基督所要在祂信徒心中造成的印象，是完全相反的。所以救主不得不說出祂從來沒有說過的最嚴厲的訓斥：“撒但退我後邊去吧，你是絆我腳的，因為你不體貼上帝的意思，只體貼人的意思。”

彼得热爱他的主，但是耶稣没有因彼得这样表示渴望保护祂脱离苦难而称赞他。彼得的话，在耶稣面临的大试炼中，并不足以使祂得到帮助和安慰。这些话并不符合上帝对于失丧世界所有恩典的旨意，也不符合耶稣来用自己的榜样所发挥自我牺牲的教训。彼得不愿意在基督的工作上看到一个十字架。彼得这些话所造成的印象，与基督所要在祂信徒心中造成的印象，是完全相反的。所以救主不得不说出祂从来没有说过的最严厉的训斥：“撒但退我后边去吧，你是绊我脚的，因为你不体贴上帝的意思，只体贴人的意思。”

Satan was trying to discourage Jesus, and turn Him from His mission; and Peter, in his blind love, was giving voice to the temptation. The prince of evil was the author of the thought. His instigation was behind that impulsive appeal. In the wilderness, Satan had offered Christ the dominion of the world on condition of forsaking the path of humiliation and sacrifice. Now he was presenting the same temptation to the disciple of Christ. He was seeking to fix Peter’s gaze upon the earthly glory, that he might not behold the cross to which Jesus desired to turn his eyes. And through Peter, Satan was again pressing the temptation upon Jesus. But the Saviour heeded it not; His thought was for His disciple. Satan had interposed between Peter and his Master, that the heart of the disciple might not be touched at the vision of Christ’s humiliation for him. The words of Christ were spoken, not to Peter, but to the one who was trying to separate him from his Redeemer. “Get thee behind Me, Satan.” No longer interpose between Me and My erring servant. Let Me come face to face with Peter, that I may reveal to him the mystery of My love.

撒但想要使耶穌灰心喪膽，並使祂放棄祂的使命，而彼得因著盲目的愛，就為撒但的試探進言。那個思想是從邪惡之君而來的。他是在彼得背後唆使他說出那一句勸阻的話。在曠野裡，撒但曾以放棄恥辱和犧牲的途徑為條件，將世界的統治權奉送基督。現在他又把這同樣的試探施諸基督的門徒。他企圖讓彼得的視線集中屬世的榮華上，使他不看耶穌所要他仰望的十字架。而且撒但藉著彼得，又將試探放在耶穌面前。但是救主毫不動心。祂是在為門徒著想。撒但插身在彼得和他的夫子之間，使彼得不因基督為他所受的凌辱而感動。基督以下的話，不是對彼得講的，乃是對那企圖離間彼得和救贖主的惡者講的：“撒但退我後邊去吧，”不要再插身在我和我這有過失的僕人中間。讓我和彼得面對面，把我慈愛的奧秘啟示給他。

撒但想要使耶稣灰心丧胆，并使祂放弃祂的使命，而彼得因着盲目的爱，就为撒但的试探进言。那个思想是从邪恶之君而来的。他是在彼得背后唆使他说出那一句劝阻的话。在旷野里，撒但曾以放弃耻辱和牺牲的途径为条件，将世界的统治权奉送基督。现在他又把这同样的试探施诸基督的门徒。他企图让彼得的视线集中属世的荣华上，使他不看耶稣所要他仰望的十字架。而且撒但借着彼得，又将试探放在耶稣面前。但是救主毫不动心。祂是在为门徒着想。撒但插身在彼得和他的夫子之间，使彼得不因基督为他所受的凌辱而感动。基督以下的话，不是对彼得讲的，乃是对那企图离间彼得和救赎主的恶者讲的：“撒但退我后边去吧，”不要再插身在我和我这有过失的仆人中间。让我和彼得面对面，把我慈爱的奥秘启示给他。

It was to Peter a bitter lesson, and one which he learned but slowly, that the path of Christ on earth lay through agony and humiliation. The disciple shrank from fellowship with his Lord in suffering. But in the heat of the furnace fire he was to learn its blessing. Long afterward, when his active form was bowed with the burden of years and labors, he wrote, “Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you: but rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when His glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.” 1 Peter 4:12, 13.

這對於彼得是一個慘痛的教訓。而且他只能慢慢地學會這個教訓，就是基督在地上的道路，是要經過痛苦和恥辱的。彼得怕與他的主同受苦難。但是他要在窯中火勢最烈的時候，體會到與主同受苦難的福分。多年以後，在他年邁力衰，老態龍鍾的時候，他寫道：“親愛的弟兄啊，有火煉的試驗臨到你們，不要以為奇怪，似乎是遭遇非常的事，倒要歡喜，因為你們是與基督一同受苦，使你們在祂榮耀顯現的時候，也可以歡喜快樂”（彼前4:12,13）。

这对于彼得是一个惨痛的教训。而且他只能慢慢地学会这个教训，就是基督在地上的道路，是要经过痛苦和耻辱的。彼得怕与他的主同受苦难。但是他要在窑中火势最烈的时候，体会到与主同受苦难的福分。多年以后，在他年迈力衰，老态龙钟的时候，他写道：“亲爱的弟兄啊，有火炼的试验临到你们，不要以为奇怪，似乎是遭遇非常的事，倒要欢喜，因为你们是与基督一同受苦，使你们在祂荣耀显现的时候，也可以欢喜快乐”（彼前4:12,13）。

Jesus now explained to His disciples that His own life of self-abnegation was an example of what theirs should be. Calling about Him, with the disciples, the people who had been lingering near, He said, “If any man will come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow Me.” The cross was associated with the power of Rome. It was the instrument of the most cruel and humiliating form of death. The lowest criminals were required to bear the cross to the place of execution; and often as it was about to be laid upon their shoulders, they resisted with desperate violence, until they were overpowered, and the instrument of torture was bound upon them. But Jesus bade His followers take up the cross and bear it after Him. To the disciples His words, though dimly comprehended, pointed to their submission to the most bitter humiliation,—submission even unto death for the sake of Christ. No more complete self-surrender could the Saviour’s words have pictured. But all this He had accepted for them. Jesus did not count heaven a place to be desired while we were lost. He left the heavenly courts for a life of reproach and insult, and a death of shame. He who was rich in heaven’s priceless treasure, became poor, that through His poverty we might be rich. We are to follow in the path He trod.

於是耶穌對祂的門徒解釋，祂捨己為人的生活乃是他們生活的榜樣。祂又召集祂的門徒和那些留戀在祂旁邊的一些人，向他們說：“若有人要跟從我，就當捨己，背起他的十字架，來跟從我。”十字架是與羅馬人的威權相連，是最殘酷最屈辱的死刑工具。窮兇極惡的犯人必須自己把十字架背到刑場，往往當十字架將要放在他們肩上時，他們就極其兇暴地加以抗拒，直到被人制伏，將刑具綁在他們的身上為止。但是耶穌吩咐跟從祂的人，要背起十字架來跟從祂。門徒對於祂的話雖然沒有完全領悟，但多少明白這話是意味著他們必須忍受最難堪的恥辱；為基督的緣故甘心忍受以至於死。救主描述捨己的話，不能比這更透徹的了。但這一切，耶穌都已經定意要為他們的緣故忍受了。當我們失迷的時候，耶穌並沒有以天國為可羨慕的地方。祂離開天庭，來度受辱的生活，遭受可恥的慘死。祂本來富有天國無價的財寶，卻成了貧窮，叫我們因祂的貧窮可以成為富足。我們要隨著祂所走過的道路前進。

于是耶稣对祂的门徒解释，祂舍己为人的生活乃是他们生活的榜样。祂又召集祂的门徒和那些留恋在祂旁边的一些人，向他们说：“若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，背起他的十字架，来跟从我。”十字架是与罗马人的威权相连，是最残酷最屈辱的死刑工具。穷凶极恶的犯人必须自己把十字架背到刑场，往往当十字架将要放在他们肩上时，他们就极其凶暴地加以抗拒，直到被人制伏，将刑具绑在他们的身上为止。但是耶稣吩咐跟从祂的人，要背起十字架来跟从祂。门徒对于祂的话虽然没有完全领悟，但多少明白这话是意味着他们必须忍受最难堪的耻辱；为基督的缘故甘心忍受以至于死。救主描述舍己的话，不能比这更透彻的了。但这一切，耶稣都已经定意要为他们的缘故忍受了。当我们失迷的时候，耶稣并没有以天国为可羡慕的地方。祂离开天庭，来度受辱的生活，遭受可耻的惨死。祂本来富有天国无价的财宝，却成了贫穷，叫我们因祂的贫穷可以成为富足。我们要随着祂所走过的道路前进。

Love for souls for whom Christ died means crucifixion of self. He who is a child of God should henceforth look upon himself as a link in the chain let down to save the world, one with Christ in His plan of mercy, going forth with Him to seek and save the lost. The Christian is ever to realize that he has consecrated himself to God, and that in character he is to reveal Christ to the world. The self-sacrifice, the sympathy, the love, manifested in the life of Christ are to reappear in the life of the worker for God.
我們若愛基督所替死的人，就必須把自己也釘在十字架上。凡是上帝的兒女，從今以後該看自己是上天垂下拯救世人的鏈子上的一環，在基督救恩的計劃上與祂合而為一，與祂一同前去尋找拯救失喪的人。基督徒應當時刻覺得自己已經獻身給上帝，而且在品格上要向世人表現基督。基督一生所顯示的自我犧牲、同情和仁愛，應當在為上帝工作之人的生活上重新表現出來。
我们若爱基督所替死的人，就必须把自己也钉在十字架上。凡是上帝的儿女，从今以后该看自己是上天垂下拯救世人的链子上的一环，在基督救恩的计划上与祂合而为一，与祂一同前去寻找拯救失丧的人。基督徒应当时刻觉得自己已经献身给上帝，而且在品格上要向世人表现基督。基督一生所显示的自我牺牲、同情和仁爱，应当在为上帝工作之人的生活上重新表现出来。

“Whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for My sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.” Selfishness is death. No organ of the body could live should it confine its service to itself. The heart, failing to send its lifeblood to the hand and the head, would quickly lose its power. As our lifeblood, so is the love of Christ diffused through every part of His mystical body. We are members one of another, and the soul that refuses to impart will perish. And “what is a man profited,” said Jesus, “if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?”
